report.summary: This release changes how the console logging library handles repeated log messages, so console output produced through it should be re-verified wherever the library is used.
keyChanges: Identical log messages emitted in quick succession inside the library's throttle window are no longer silently dropped: when the next different message is logged, the suppressed message is printed once more with a count appended, so logging the same message three times quickly and then a different one now also prints a copy annotated '(repeated 2 times)', where the number is the count of suppressed repeats (two quick copies yield '(repeated 1 times)'); previously the repeats vanished with no trace.
The repetition notice only appears once a later, non-suppressed log is emitted, so a burst of identical messages that is the last thing logged still produces no extra line, same as before.

Every logger instance now initializes its own last-log tracking and repeat counter at creation, including loggers created through the library's factory methods with preset defaults or tags, so the new counting behavior applies consistently wherever the library logs, in server and browser builds alike.
qaChecks: Test: log the same message three times in quick succession and then log a different message; verify the console shows the repeated message once more with the exact text '(repeated 2 times)' appended after its original content, followed by the different message.

Check: with a single suppressed repeat (same message logged twice quickly, then a different message), verify the notice reads '(repeated 1 times)' and the repeated line keeps its original log level, tag, and message text with only the note added.

Ensure: two different messages logged back-to-back within the throttle window both print normally with no repetition note, and a burst of identical messages that is the final output produces no extra line.

Confirm: run the duplicate-message scenario separately on a logger created with preset defaults or a tag and verify it counts its own repeats from zero at creation and shows the '(repeated N times)' note when its next different message is logged.
Verify: a repeat burst on one logger followed by logging from a different logger does not attach the first logger's pending repetition note to the other logger's output.
uncertainty: The repetition note is appended as an extra final element of the log's arguments, so any consumer that reads, formats, or matches log arguments exactly, such as custom log reporters, log collectors, or checks asserting exact console output, now receives an additional trailing string; since no application context was supplied, QA should spot-check any in-app log display or log-based assertions still handle the note.

report.summary: Repeated identical log entries within the throttle window are now counted and reported once as a single summary line with a repeat count, replacing the previous behavior of silently dropping duplicates.
keyChanges: When the same log entry with identical type, tag, and arguments is emitted repeatedly within the throttle window, the logger now counts every suppressed duplicate instead of only silently discarding it.

When a different log entry is next emitted, the logger first outputs one summary line for the suppressed entry with a suffix such as (repeated 5 times) stating the exact number of hidden duplicates before writing the new entry.
The repeat counter resets to zero after each summary is flushed, so later bursts of duplicates are reported independently from earlier ones.

Every newly created logger initializes its repeat count and log-tracking state to empty values at creation time, and identical consecutive log entries that differ in type, tag, or arguments are never counted as duplicates.
qaChecks: Verify that emitting the exact same log entry with the same type, tag, and arguments several times within the throttle window produces no output during the suppression period.

Confirm that the first different log entry emitted afterwards is preceded by one flushed line of the suppressed entry carrying a suffix such as (repeated 5 times) that matches the exact number of hidden duplicates.
Check that after a summary line is flushed, a new burst of identical duplicates starts counting from 1 again rather than accumulating onto the previous count.
Ensure that a log entry whose type, tag, or arguments differ from the previous one is treated as new content and never counted as a duplicate.
Confirm that a freshly created logger initializes without errors and logs normally, with the repeated-times summary appearing only after identical consecutive entries were suppressed.

report.summary: A logging-library change now surfaces throttled duplicate messages with a repeat count instead of dropping them silently, making rapid repeated log output the main QA focus.
keyChanges: Duplicate log messages emitted within the throttling window are no longer discarded without a trace: each repeat is now counted, and when the next different message is logged, the suppressed message is printed again with '(repeated N times)' appended after its original arguments. Previously the duplicates vanished silently.

To support this, every logger now initializes its repeat-tracking state (last log, its serialized form, its timestamp, and a repeat counter starting at zero) when created, so derived loggers such as tagged or defaults-based variants start counting repeats from zero.

The low-level log writer now receives a re-emitted copy of the last logged message with one extra trailing text argument when a repeat summary is flushed, so any formatting of log arguments will see that additional text.
qaChecks: Verify that logging the exact same message several times in quick succession (for example 'save failed' three times back to back) followed by a different message prints the original message once, then the same message again with '(repeated 2 times)' appended, then the different message; under the previous behavior the duplicates disappeared with no note.

Check the single-duplicate case: log one message twice in quick succession and then a different message; the summary line should read '(repeated 1 times)' exactly, placed at the end of the repeated message, with all original arguments intact including multiple arguments or an object argument.
Confirm that if the duplicated message is the last thing logged, no repeat summary appears until a different message is logged afterwards.

Verify that repeating the same tagged message rapidly and then logging a different message shows the repeat summary with the tag still attached and the correct count, and that each derived logger's count starts at zero so repeats in one logger do not inflate another logger's first summary.
uncertainty: When a repeat is suppressed after a different message was printed outside the throttling window, the summary may be attached to the most recently printed line rather than the line that actually repeated, because the duplicate baseline is not refreshed by out-of-window messages; note which message carries the '(repeated N times)' text whenever a repeat sequence spans a throttling gap.

report.summary: This release rebuilds how the logging library assembles its default logger by sharing one instance on the global object in Node and browser builds, activating seven previously disabled legacy method shortcuts, and switching several exports to named-only, so QA should confirm logging still works end to end and that existing import styles still resolve.
keyChanges: The main Node entry now builds and exports a ready-to-use default logger instance and stores it on the global object, applying the previous platform rules: debug level in debug mode, warn level in test runs, info level otherwise, an optional numeric CONSOLA_LEVEL override that falls back to the default for non-numeric values, and a plain reporter in CI or test runs versus the styled fancy reporter locally.

A new browser entry builds the default logger with the browser reporter and shares it on the global object, reusing an already present global logger instead of replacing it, while the old platform-specific entry modules no longer export anything.

Seven legacy method shortcuts for adding and removing reporters, clearing all reporters, setting a scope tag, mocking log types, and pausing and resuming output were activated after previously being only comments, so calls using those older names now work where they previously failed as missing methods.

The public export shape changed: the logger class and the log-type definitions became named-only exports, a new factory for building custom loggers was added, and reporters are no longer re-exported from the package root, so default-style imports of the class or types and direct named imports of reporters now resolve to nothing and dependent code still using them breaks at runtime.
qaChecks: Verify importing the main entry yields a working default logger whose messages appear on the console and that separate imports return the same single instance stored on the global object.

Test CONSOLA_LEVEL with a numeric value such as 3, which must be honored by changing which messages print, and with a non-numeric value such as verbose, which must fall back to the default level rather than silencing everything or crashing.
Confirm reporter selection: in a CI or test run the log output appears in plain format, and in a normal local run it appears in the styled fancy format.

Verify the browser bundle exposes exactly one shared logger on the global object: importing the entry twice returns the same instance, and a logger already present on the global object is reused rather than replaced.
Verify logging from browser code writes messages to the browser console through the browser reporter.
uncertainty: Which files the published package entry points now resolve to is not confirmed because no build or package configuration was supplied; if any entry still resolves to an emptied module, consumers would load nothing at all, which should be verified against the built package before release.

report.summary: The logging library restructured its package entry points and export surface around a new factory for building logger instances, re-enabled legacy logging call styles, and kept environment-based reporter and log-level behavior, with no application screens or navigation supplied for testing.
keyChanges: The Node and browser package entries were rebuilt so importing the library now creates the default logger and assigns it to the global object only if none exists, using the browser reporter in browsers and, on Node, the plain basic reporter in CI or test runs versus the fancy formatted reporter in development.

Default log level stays Info (Debug in debug mode, Warn under test) with an optional CONSOLA_LEVEL override where zero or non-numeric values fall back to the default, and this logic simply moved from the old Node-specific entry with no behavior change.

Legacy logging call styles for registering, removing, clearing, scope tagging, mocking, pausing, and resuming were re-activated as aliases of their canonical methods, so these shorter call styles now work at runtime instead of being dormant.
A newly exported factory function now builds custom logger instances from partial options, and the set of log type definitions is exported by name instead of as a default with unchanged contents.

The package export surface narrowed: the root entry no longer re-exports the reporter classes, the logger class lost its default export in favor of a named one, and the root now also default-exports the ready logger instance.
qaChecks: Verify a default import of the package returns a working logger that prints an info-level message with fancy formatting in a normal development environment and registers itself as the global logger.

Confirm that under a CI or test environment the same import logs through the plain basic reporter instead, and that the default level hides info messages under test while showing debug messages in debug mode.
Validate the CONSOLA_LEVEL override with a valid numeric level filtering output as set, and with zero or a non-numeric value falling back to the environment default without crashing.

Test the alias call styles that were previously inactive: registering a reporter through the registering alias should make it receive subsequent log messages like the canonical method, and the clearing alias should make registered reporters stop receiving logs.

Check pausing and resuming: after pausing, a logged message produces no output and after resuming output continues; confirm the tagging and mocking aliases add tag or type overrides the same way as their canonical methods.
uncertainty: The package root no longer re-exports the reporter classes, so downstream code importing them the old way will break, and the supplied context gives no consumer information to judge how likely that is.

report.summary: This release adds a new interactive command-line prompting capability to the consola library, so QA must check that text, confirm, single-select, and multi-select prompts work from the terminal on both the Node and browser entry points while ordinary log output still works.
keyChanges: The library can now be asked a question from the terminal via the new prompt method, covering text input, yes/no confirmation, single-choice selection, and multi-choice selection where answering nothing can be allowed or blocked.

Both entry points provide prompting differently: the Node entry point lazily loads the shared prompt implementation and forwards all arguments, while the browser entry point implements prompting locally with a browser confirm dialog for yes/no questions and a plain text prompt for everything else.
The instance now stores the prompt implementation passed at construction time, so a logger built without prompting support throws a clear error when a question is asked rather than doing nothing.
Ordinary log-level filtering in the core logger is unchanged despite a small type-cast edit, so existing logging behavior needs a regression pass since every log call flows through it.

The shared package surface was refactored so the logger factory is exported directly from each platform entry point instead of being re-exported from shared code, which may affect how downstream consumers reach it.
qaChecks: Check the four prompts in sequence: enter a name (leaving it empty once to see the 'Not sure' placeholder behavior), answer the yes/no question, pick a project type including the duplicate TypeScript entry and the CoffeeScript entry showing its hint, and multi-select the three tool options; each answer should return the expected value without errors.
Test the multi-select with answering nothing allowed by pressing enter with nothing selected; it should submit successfully with an empty selection and no validation error.
Confirm the single-choice list accepts plain string options and shows the given hint text next to the highlighted option.
Verify asking a question through a logger built by the main package factory loads the prompting capability lazily and shows the question in the terminal, rather than failing.
Verify a confirm-type prompt opens the browser confirm dialog and resolves to the chosen boolean, while a default text prompt opens the browser prompt dialog and resolves to the typed value.
uncertainty: No application context or annotated surfaces exist for this repository, so navigation instructions come from the code examples and entry-point structure rather than verified documentation; additionally, the browser prompt ignores every option except the question type, so browser-specific options such as placeholder or default values are silently not applied and QA should confirm whether that gap matters to downstream users.

report.summary: This release consolidates the logging library's Node and browser entry points into shared main entries that publish a global default logger, moves to a named-only export surface, and re-enables legacy logging shortcuts, so QA should focus on import compatibility, per-environment console output, log-level overrides, and the pause-and-resume flow.
keyChanges: Importing the main Node or browser entry now creates one shared logger instance and publishes it as the global logger, reusing any logger the host already set: Node picks a plain reporter under CI or test conditions and a formatted reporter otherwise, the browser entry uses the browser reporter, and the old dedicated Node and browser entry modules were removed.

The default log level is Debug under debug mode, Warn under test mode, and Info otherwise, and the CONSOLA_LEVEL environment variable can override it, with values that do not parse as a number, including 0, falling back to the default level.

The public export surface changed: the logger class and the log-type map are now named exports only because their default exports were removed, reporter classes are no longer re-exported from the main entry, and a new factory for building custom logger instances is exported.

Shortcut methods for common logging actions, such as adding, removing, or clearing log output destinations, tagging or scoping messages, mocking output, and pausing or resuming logging, were previously left unassigned and are now active aliases of their newer equivalents, so pausing queues messages and resuming flushes them.
qaChecks: Verify info-level messages print to the terminal with the formatted reporter in a normal run and switch to the plain reporter output when a CI or test environment is detected.
Verify that with no CONSOLA_LEVEL set, warning messages appear while debug messages stay hidden, matching the Info default.
Verify that with CONSOLA_LEVEL=0 and then CONSOLA_LEVEL=verbose in separate runs, the logger falls back to the default level so info messages still appear instead of going silent or failing to start.

Confirm the consumer app or demo starts without import or build errors using the new named exports, since the logger class and the log-type map no longer provide default exports and reporters are no longer re-exported from the main entry.
Verify logging works end to end from the main Node and browser entries wherever the removed dedicated entries were used before.
uncertainty: No application context, pages, or navigation were supplied, so the consumer applications and user-facing surfaces affected by this library could not be identified; the removal of default exports and the reporter re-exports is breaking for any consumer that used the old import style, and which consumers those are is unknown.

report.summary: This release adds interactive prompt support (text, confirm, select, multi-select) to the logging library for terminals and browsers, restructures how logger instances are created, and ships a demo script; existing logging output is not expected to change.
keyChanges: A new prompt feature lets the logger ask interactive questions: free text (with placeholder and pre-filled value), a yes/no confirm that defaults to Yes, a single-choice list where plain strings become both label and value and options can show hints, and a multi-choice list that can be marked optional.

Unknown prompt types are rejected with an 'Unknown prompt type' error, and a logger created without prompt support throws 'prompt is not supported!' when its prompt method is called; in Node the prompt module is loaded on demand on first use.

Multi-select prompts require at least one selection by default, showing 'Please select at least one option.' with a space/enter hint when submitted empty, unless the caller marks the prompt optional, as the demo does.

The logger factory is now exported directly from both the Node and browser entry points (no longer re-exported through the shared module), accepts an options object, and applies environment-based default reporters (plain in CI/test, styled locally, browser reporter in the browser) that callers can override.

A new demo script walks through all four prompt types, including a list with 'TypeScript' listed twice and a hinted 'CoffeeScript' option; in browsers, confirm prompts open the native OK/Cancel dialog and all other prompts open the native input dialog.

Terminal prompts render unicode symbols with ASCII fallbacks on terminals without unicode support, and multi-select requires at least one selection by default unless the caller passes required as false.

report.summary: This release reworks Excalidraw's drawing list to immutable handling across nearly all canvas interactions, changing undo/redo data flow, paste placement, mouse selection rules, and file/browser-storage loading.
keyChanges: Undo (Ctrl/Cmd+Z) and redo (Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z) now receive the restored snapshot as a returned drawing state that the editor adopts, and a corrupt history entry no longer throws but results in no change.

Nearly every canvas operation (delete, clear, deselect, arrow-key nudging, select all, adding shapes and text, Alt-duplication, layer reordering, and style changes) now rebuilds the drawing list instead of editing it in place, so all basic drawing flows need re-verification even though the visible actions are unchanged.

Pasting keeps the copied shapes' original coordinates and shifts them by the paste offset instead of re-anchoring the group's top-left corner at the target, so pasted content lands in different places than in the previous release.

Mouse-down selection changed: the editor first hit-tests only already-selected shapes, so Shift-clicking empty canvas no longer clears the selection, and clicking an unselected shape overlapping a selected one may add to the selection instead of replacing it.

Scene loading and browser-storage restore use a new data pipeline: opening a malformed file now resolves to an empty drawing (previously the current drawing was left untouched), and corrupt stored data silently yields empty content.
qaChecks: Verify Ctrl/Cmd+Z steps back one action at a time through adding, moving, styling, and deleting shapes, and Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z re-applies each step in the same order.
Ensure pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Z (and Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z) when there is nothing to undo or redo, such as right after opening the editor, changes nothing and shows no error.
Confirm that after undoing everything and redoing it, the canvas and the autosaved browser state match the original drawing.

Verify pasting a multi-shape copy places the pasted copies fully visible on screen with their relative arrangement preserved; the anchor logic changed, so the paste location will differ from the previous release.
Test pasting shapes that were copied far from the canvas origin and pasting onto an empty canvas: the pasted content should still appear in a sensible, reachable position rather than far off-screen.
uncertainty: The paste offset rework (the previous top-left normalization was removed and its calculation commented out) means the intended target position for pasted content is not established by the supplied context; confirm with product where pasted shapes should land, especially when pasting content copied from a distant location or onto an empty canvas.

report.summary: This release reworks the drawing editor's internal data handling to immutable updates, visibly changing paste placement, loading of invalid files, and shift-click selection while aiming to keep undo/redo and everyday editing behavior unchanged.
keyChanges: The editor now rebuilds the drawing's element list instead of editing it in place for selection, deletion, stacking-order moves, property edits, undo/redo, and pasting, so all canvas interactions need a smoke test even though the intended visible behavior is the same.
Undo and redo now return the restored drawing snapshot directly, and when there is nothing left to undo or redo the drawing is left untouched.

Loading a drawing file or restoring from browser storage is more tolerant: a corrupt file no longer crashes the app, but an invalid file now clears the canvas where it previously had no effect, and partially corrupt browser storage no longer wipes shapes whose data still parses.
Pasted shapes now land relative to the paste point regardless of where the originals were drawn; previously the paste position depended on the originals' coordinates.
Canvas click handling was restructured: clicking empty canvas still clears the selection, but shift-clicking empty canvas now keeps the current selection, which it previously cleared.

Verify pressing undo repeatedly removes the last actions one by one and redo re-applies them in the original order.
Test pressing undo after the history is exhausted: the canvas must remain unchanged with no error and no accidental clearing.
uncertainty: Loading an invalid drawing file now replaces the canvas with an empty scene, whereas an invalid file previously had no effect on the drawing; whether this destructive outcome is intended was not established by the supplied evidence.

report.summary: This release rebuilds how the drawing canvas stores and updates its elements (immutable copies instead of in-place edits) across undo/redo, selection, pasting, file handling, and styling, so all core editing workflows on the Excalidraw canvas need a regression pass.
keyChanges: Undo and redo now apply a restored copy of the drawing returned by history (an empty history is a silent no-op) instead of editing the shared element list in place.
Escape, Delete, Cut, select-all, arrow-key nudging, and every style or property edit now replace the element list with a new copy, so each of these must still visibly behave exactly as before.
Pasting copied elements no longer re-anchors them to the copied group's top-left corner, so pastes of drawings made far from the canvas origin now land further away and may appear off-screen.

Opening a scene file or restoring browser-saved data now tolerates bad data: an invalid or non-scene file silently resets the canvas to empty, whereas previously a failed load left the existing drawing untouched; page reload still restores the last drawing.
Layer reordering, paste-styles (including text font), double-click text editing, and the clear-canvas prompt were reworked with the same copy-based pattern and need a quick regression check.
qaChecks: Verify pressing the undo shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+Z) three times on a three-shape drawing empties the canvas, then redo (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z) three times restores all three shapes with their positions and styles intact and nothing duplicated.
Verify undo after making a fresh edit reverts that newest edit, so history keeps working after an undo (you can undo, edit, and undo again without getting stuck).
Test pressing undo with nothing left to undo and redo with an empty redo stack: the canvas must stay exactly as it is with no freeze, error, or unwanted history step.
Verify saving the drawing to a file and re-opening it restores every element with its styles, including defaults (hachure fill, stroke width 1, roughness 1, opacity 100) for fields the file omits.

Test opening the invalid file while the canvas holds unsaved work: the app must stay responsive with no crash, but expect the canvas to be reset to empty — this silently discards the current drawing, a behavior change from previous builds that left the drawing untouched on a failed load.
uncertainty: Pasting no longer re-anchors copied elements to the group's top-left corner, so pastes of drawings made far from the canvas origin land shifted and may go off-screen; the change looks deliberate but the intended placement was not documented, so confirm the expected paste position with the team before sign-off.

report.summary: This Excalidraw release reworks how the editor's element properties panel reads values and how text elements are created and edited, with the opacity control's new 100 default and 0-value handling as the top regression risk.
keyChanges: All element property controls (stroke color, background color, fill style, stroke width, sloppiness, opacity, font size, font family) now read their displayed value through one shared rule: prefer the element currently being edited, then the value only if every selected element shares it, otherwise a fallback default or blank.

The opacity control changed its fallback when selected elements have no shared opacity: it now shows the default 100 instead of the old 0, and because the new logic treats 0 as 'no value', an element truly set to 0% opacity can now display as 100% in the panel — the top regression to verify.
Confirming the text editor with empty text no longer adds a text element to the canvas, so empty text boxes should no longer be left behind or duplicated when a text edit is abandoned.
Double-clicking an existing text element now edits that element in place, pre-filled with its current text and its own font, and rebuilds it with recalculated size and centered position on confirm.
The color pickers were updated to accept a null (no shared color) state, matching the new no-common-value behavior for stroke and background colors.
qaChecks: Test setting a shape's opacity to 0 (drag the opacity field fully left or enter 0), deselect it, then reselect it: the opacity field should still show 0 and the shape should stay invisible; with this change the field may wrongly show 100 because a 0 value is treated as empty.

Verify selecting two shapes with different opacities (for example 50 and 80) now shows the default 100 in the opacity field instead of the previous 0, and that entering a new opacity applies to both shapes.
Confirm that after any opacity change, undo restores the elements' previous opacity values on canvas.
Test picking the text tool, clicking on empty canvas, and confirming with no text typed (empty confirm or Escape): no empty text box should be left on the canvas.
Verify typing text and confirming creates the text centered on the click point with a box that fits the text, without the text appearing offset from where you clicked.
uncertainty: The intended outcome when clearing all text from an existing text element and confirming is not established by the evidence: the new behavior simply adds nothing, so record whether the original element is kept, removed, or duplicated and raise it if an empty box or a duplicate text element appears.

report.summary: This release reworks text creation and editing on the canvas and how the element properties panel derives its values, changing what mixed or zero-value selections display and stopping empty text elements from being added.
keyChanges: Element properties are now read through a new helper that prefers the element currently being edited, then the value shared by all selected elements (empty when they differ), then the tool default; while a text editor is open the panel now reflects the text being edited.

For opacity, a selection with conflicting values now shows the 100 default in the slider where the old code showed 0, and because 0 now counts as an empty value, a genuinely fully transparent element is expected to display 100 in the slider.

Text creation was rebuilt around a new text-element factory: submitting the text editor with no text no longer adds an invisible empty text element, and text elements are measured and centered when created.
Double-clicking an existing text element now opens that element itself for editing, pre-filled with its current text and font, instead of layering a new element over it.
Color picker internals now carry an explicit null empty state instead of undefined; this is mostly plumbing, but element and canvas background picking should be re-verified.
qaChecks: Verify that with the text tool you click the canvas and submit the empty editor with Enter: nothing is added to the canvas, whereas before this change an invisible empty text element was left behind.
Check that typing text after a single click and submitting produces exactly one text element, sized to the text and centered on the point where you clicked, with no upward or sideways offset.

Verify that double-clicking an existing text element opens the editor pre-filled with its current text, and that after changing the text and submitting, the canvas holds one updated text element at the same position with no leftover copy of the old text.
Confirm that while the text editor is open, the properties panel shows the color and font of the text being edited rather than the generic tool defaults.
Verify that selecting a single shape shows that shape's actual stroke color, background color, fill style, stroke width, sloppiness, and opacity in the panel, unchanged from before.
uncertainty: When an existing text element is edited by double-clicking, the new flow rebuilds the element when the text editor is submitted and appends it to the drawing, and the diff does not show the pre-edit original being removed; double-check that editing existing text does not leave a stale duplicate of the old text overlapping the new one, and report it if it does.

report.summary: Pasting spreadsheet data into the drawing canvas now also accepts comma-separated (CSV) data, invalid spreadsheet pastes no longer show error messages and fall back to a text paste, and generated charts are redesigned with axis lines, a centered title, taller bars, fixed default styling and single-group selection instead of following the current drawing styles.
keyChanges: Pasted data that is not tab-separated into exactly two columns is now re-parsed as comma-separated, so two-column CSV text pastes create a bar chart where the previous release rejected it.

Data with more than two columns or with no numeric column no longer returns an error message (previously errors for too many columns or no numeric column were shown); it is now treated as not a spreadsheet and falls through to a normal text paste on the canvas.

Generated charts are redesigned: bar height increased from 192 to 256, the chart gains x- and y-axis lines plus a dotted line at the maximum value, the header row becomes a centered title above the chart instead of a rotated y-axis label, and all chart parts share one group so selecting any part selects the whole chart.

Charts no longer adopt the current drawing styles (stroke color, background, fill style, stroke width, roughness, opacity, font); they use fixed defaults with a background color chosen at random from the built-in palette.

Creating a chart now fires a new analytics event (category 'magic', name 'chart', value equal to the bar count) when analytics is enabled; the remaining changes are internal refactorings and type-only updates with no user-visible behavior.
qaChecks: Test pasting two-column comma-separated data (a small CSV file or text, for example a header 'Month,Value' plus rows 'Jan,10' and 'Feb,20'): a bar chart should be created on the canvas; this input was rejected before this change.

Verify pasting a two-column tab-separated selection with a header row copied from Excel or Google Sheets still creates a chart, now with the header as a centered title above the chart, x- and y-axis lines, a dotted line at the maximum value, a 0 at the axis base, and taller bars (height 256 instead of 192).
Verify that creating a chart from a paste records one chart analytics event whose value equals the number of bars pasted, when analytics is enabled in the test environment.

Test pasting a tab-separated selection with three or more columns copied from Excel: the content should be pasted onto the canvas as a normal text element and no error message should appear; the previous release showed an error about too many columns.
Check pasting two columns of words with no numbers: it should paste as text with no error message; the previous release showed an error about a missing numeric column.
uncertainty: Charts built from data containing negative values: the previous chart offset bars from a minimum baseline (the lower of 0 and the smallest value), so negative values rendered above the baseline; the new chart divides each value by the maximum only, so a negative value produces a negative bar height. Paste data that includes a negative number among positive values (for example -5) and record whether the chart still renders correctly; treat any corrupted or missing bars as a regression of this release.

report.summary: This release reworks the paste-a-spreadsheet chart feature: comma-separated data now creates bar charts, generated charts are visibly restyled (fixed colors, axis lines, grouped elements, centered title, taller bars), and invalid spreadsheet pastes no longer show dedicated error messages.
keyChanges: Pasting two columns of comma-separated data into the drawing canvas now creates a bar chart; previously only tab-separated data (copied from spreadsheet apps) was recognized, and tab-separated pastes continue to work.

Data with more than two columns or with no numeric column no longer produces a dedicated error message (the old 'too many columns' and 'no numeric column' errors are gone); such content is now treated like any non-spreadsheet paste and is inserted as text instead.

Generated charts are different to look at: bars are taller (chart height raised from 192 to 256) and scale as value divided by the maximum from a zero baseline with a '0' label, new x and y axis lines plus a dotted maximum-value line are drawn, and the value column's header appears as a centered title above the chart instead of a label at its left side.

Charts no longer follow the toolbar's stroke, fill, and font selections: each pasted chart uses fixed default styling with one background color picked at random from the palette, and the whole chart is created as a single group, so selecting, moving, or deleting any part now affects the entire chart.
qaChecks: Verify pasting two columns of comma-separated data creates a bar chart with one bar per data row; this previously pasted as plain text because only tab-separated data was recognized.
Verify pasting two tab-separated columns copied from a spreadsheet app still creates a bar chart with the correct number of bars and bar heights matching the pasted values.
Verify that with a header row, the value column's header appears as a title centered above the chart; it previously appeared as a label at the left of the chart.

Verify pasting two columns that include a negative value still renders a usable chart: the previous release drew negative bars below the axis and labeled the axis start with the lowest value, so flag inverted or overlapping bars, a wrong baseline label, or an error as a regression.

Verify pasting tab-separated data with three or more columns is handled like a normal non-spreadsheet paste (content inserted as text, no chart) and no dedicated 'too many columns' error message appears; the previous release showed one.
uncertainty: Expected behavior for negative values in pasted charts is unresolved: the previous release scaled bars from the data minimum and supported negative bars below the axis, while the new code divides each value by the maximum and always labels the baseline '0', so the negative-value check documents what to watch for (a crash, inverted or overlapping bars, or a wrong baseline label).

report.summary: This release adds a toggleable scene statistics panel to the Excalidraw canvas context menu, with the toggle remembered across reloads but excluded from exported files, alongside internal cleanups that warrant light regression checks on element properties.
keyChanges: A new stats panel opens from the canvas right-click context menu; it shows scene element count, width and height, and browser-storage sizes in compact k/M/G-style formatting, and when elements are selected it shows either a single element's position, size, and angle or a selected count with combined bounds.
The stats on/off state defaults to off, is preserved in browser storage across page reloads and when clearing the canvas, but is not written into exported or saved drawing files.

The selection helper used by the sharpness property and the selected-shape actions (desktop properties panel and mobile menu) was renamed; behavior is unchanged, but those paths now run through the new helper.
Total browser-storage size now reuses a shared helper with identical math, and the debounce utility gained a cancel method used by the new panel; neither is expected to change existing behavior.
qaChecks: Verify the context menu shows the new stats entry and selecting it opens the panel; choosing it again or using the panel's close control hides it.

Verify with nothing selected the panel shows scene totals (element count, width, height, storage sizes) with no selected-element section; with exactly one shape selected it shows that element's position, size, and angle; with two or more selected it shows a selected-elements count with combined position and size but no single angle.
Test an empty scene: after deleting all elements, confirm the panel still opens and shows zero elements and zero storage sizes without errors or blank cells.
Verify the other context-menu entries (for example the grid toggle) still work and the new stats entry displays a readable localized label rather than a raw translation key.
Verify that turning the panel on and reloading the page reopens it, and turning it off and reloading keeps it closed.
uncertainty: The exact wording of the new menu entry and panel strings comes from translation keys not included in the supplied context, so whether every supported language provides the new stats label is unconfirmed; flag any language where the entry renders as a raw key.

report.summary: This release overhauls the paste-spreadsheet-to-chart feature: charts get a redesigned look with axis lines and grouping, comma-separated data is newly recognized, unchartable data no longer shows error messages, and chart creation now sends an analytics event.
keyChanges: Pasting spreadsheet text now also accepts comma-separated data, not only tab-separated, so comma-based rows create bar charts where they previously were not recognized as a chart at all.

Charts are drawn differently: new horizontal and vertical axis lines, a dotted line marking the maximum value, a title above the chart instead of a rotated label on the left side, bars scaled from a zero baseline, and all chart pieces grouped so selecting one piece selects the whole chart.

Charts no longer copy the colors and styles currently selected in the tool settings; they use fixed defaults with randomly chosen background colors per bar, and the bar area is taller than before (192 to 256).
Data that cannot become a chart (more than two columns, or no numeric column) no longer shows the specific error messages it used to; it is silently treated as normal paste content.
Creating a chart now fires an analytics event recording the number of bars, and negative values take a new scaling path that assumes a zero baseline.

Check the vertical axis labels read 0 at the origin and the maximum value at the top, and each bar height is proportional to its value measured from zero.

Test data containing a negative value mixed with positives, which the previous version handled by scaling between the smallest and largest values; confirm all bars still render sensibly with no inverted, missing, or misplaced bars.
Verify pasting two-column comma-separated data creates a bar chart; before this change only tab-separated data was recognized as a chart.
Confirm two-column tab-separated data still creates a chart as before, so the new comma fallback does not change how existing tab pastes behave.
uncertainty: The new bar scaling divides each value by the maximum against a zero baseline, while the old version scaled between the smallest and largest values; how negative values should render is not defined by this change, so if the negative-value check produces inverted or missing bars, confirm whether negative values must remain supported before release.

report.summary: This release introduces a keyboard-toggled zen mode that hides most of the drawing editor's interface chrome, and reworks how toolbar buttons are shown or hidden, so the main editor's panels, footer, and conditionally visible buttons need a regression pass.
keyChanges: A new zen mode was added to the drawing editor: pressing Alt+Z (only when Ctrl or Cmd is NOT held) turns it on and off, it defaults to off, and while it is on the left tool panel, the selected-shape panel, the bottom zoom controls and encryption indicator, the tool lock control, the footer language list and shortcuts toggle, and the GitHub corner hide or slide out of view, while a new exit-zen-mode button appears in the footer.

The keyboard shortcuts dialog now documents the new Alt+Z shortcut, and a new default app-state setting (zen mode off) flows additively into the save, load, export, and restore paths, which should not change existing saved files.

Toolbar buttons switched from an inline visibility style to CSS classes, and the class applied when a button is set to visible is literally named ToolIcon_type_button--hide (otherwise ToolIcon_type_button--show), so every button whose visibility depends on state — including the always-present zoom, undo/redo, save/open, delete/duplicate, export, and collaboration dialog buttons — must be re-verified on screen.

Shared layout pieces (the fixed side container and the floating panel surfaces) and the lock icon gained zen-mode-aware styling, and the fixed side container is also rendered by the mobile menu, so mobile layout is in scope.

Verify that exiting zen mode with Alt+Z again and by clicking the new exit-zen-mode footer button each restore every hidden panel, and that holding Ctrl or Cmd while pressing Alt+Z does not toggle zen mode.
Verify the keyboard shortcuts dialog, opened via the shortcuts control in the footer, lists a new Alt+Z entry for toggling zen mode.
Verify drawing, selecting, moving, and zooming on the canvas still work normally while zen mode is on.

Verify that all always-present toolbar buttons — the shape tool switcher, the bottom-bar zoom in/out and reset controls, undo/redo, save and open, delete and duplicate, export/copy, and the collaboration room dialog buttons — are visible and clickable in normal (non-zen) mode.
uncertainty: The reworked toolbar-button visibility now relies on stylesheet classes (ToolIcon_type_button--hide when a button is set to visible, ToolIcon_type_button--show otherwise) instead of the old inline visibility style, and the stylesheet defining those classes is not part of the supplied evidence; if any toolbar button is stuck visible or wrongly hidden in this build, this class mapping is the most likely cause and should be confirmed on screen before sign-off.

report.summary: This release reworks how the Excalidraw editor handles text attached to shapes when properties change: text-property changes now include and re-wrap the attached text with container resizing, while selection handling and panels consistently treat attached text elements.
keyChanges: Changing font size, font family, or text alignment now also applies to text bound to a selected shape (previously the attached text was skipped) and triggers a reflow: the text is re-wrapped to the container width, vertically re-centered, and the container height grows when the new text no longer fits within the available height minus padding.

While a text editor is open on attached text, the container is no longer resized immediately when properties change mid-edit; container growth now happens through the redraw step instead of during editing.

Property changes are now computed from the actual selected elements: attached text is excluded from appearance changes such as fill, stroke, opacity, stroke style and width, sloppiness, sharpness, and arrowheads by default, and included only for the three text properties.

The element targets used by the selection properties panel and the statistics panel now include attached text, so those panels can show and act on text for shapes that carry it; copy/paste styles also flow through the new reflow logic.
qaChecks: Confirm the properties panel offers text-related properties when only the shape carrying text is selected.

Verify that increasing the font size re-wraps the long attached text to the shape's width, keeps it vertically centered, and grows the shape's height to fit the text plus padding with nothing clipped outside the shape.

Ensure changing text alignment moves the attached text as expected without pushing it outside the container, and that changing the font family produces the same wrap, centering, and height growth rather than an overflowing or stale layout.
Check that while the text editor is open, changing the font size does not resize the container mid-edit and the editor does not jump or corrupt the container height.
Ensure that after finishing editing by clicking away, the container ends up sized to fit the text with no clipped text and no leftover oversized or undersized container.
uncertainty: Appearance-property changes now exclude attached text by default, while the previous code applied them to any element id present in the selection; if any existing flow placed attached text into the selection, those changes will no longer reach it, so confirm whether that exclusion is intended for all flows.

report.summary: This release reworks how the eraser is exited in the Excalidraw editor: leaving eraser mode now restores the tool used before erasing instead of always switching to selection, and Escape now exits eraser mode instead of running the deselect/finish-drawing action.
keyChanges: Pressing E while the eraser is active now switches back to the tool that was selected before the eraser (for example rectangle or text), falling back to selection only when no previous tool is recorded; previously it always switched to selection.

Pressing Escape while the eraser is active now exits eraser mode and restores the previous tool, because the keyboard action that deselects elements or finishes an in-progress drawing is now suppressed while erasing; previously Escape ran that deselect/finish action and the eraser stayed active.
A new optional editor-state field that remembers the last tool before the eraser, plus an added internal import, are supporting implementation changes with no separate user-visible effect.
qaChecks: Verify that with the rectangle tool selected, pressing E, erasing a stroke, then pressing E again switches back to the rectangle tool instead of the selection tool, and the next drag on the canvas draws a rectangle.

Verify the restored tool is the one active when E was pressed: select the text tool, press E, press E again, and confirm text mode returns; toggle E a few more times to confirm the eraser and the remembered tool keep alternating correctly.
Verify that pressing Escape while the eraser is active exits eraser mode and restores the previous tool, rather than deselecting elements while the eraser stays active as it did before.
Verify that with a non-eraser tool active, drawing a multi-point line or arrow by clicking several points and then pressing Escape or Enter finishes the element as before.
Verify that Escape still deselects currently selected elements when the eraser is not active.
uncertainty: No documented pre-change behaviour or rules were supplied for the eraser or deselect actions, so the before-versus-after comparison comes from the code diff alone; whether the eraser can ever become active through a path that does not record the previous tool, which would make exiting fall back to the selection tool, could not be established from the supplied context.

report.summary: This release adds a user-toggleable stats panel to the Excalidraw drawing editor, with supporting refactors that should not change existing behavior.
keyChanges: A new stats panel can be toggled from the drawing canvas's right-click context menu: it shows scene figures (element count, overall width and height), browser-storage figures (scene and total storage size, refreshed after about 500 milliseconds), and selection figures (x, y, width, height and angle for one selected element, or a count plus bounding-box size for several), and it closes via its own close control.

The panel's visibility is a new editor-state flag: closed by default, remembered in browser storage across page reloads, stripped from exported scene files, and carried through clear-canvas so clearing the drawing keeps the panel open.

Supporting refactors are expected to be behavior-neutral: a selection-helper rename with all callers updated, formatting-only changes to two selection helpers, a storage-size helper now reused by both the panel and the existing total-size calculation, and new number-formatting and cancellable-timing helpers that only the panel uses.
qaChecks: Verify the panel opens when you choose the new context-menu item and closes when you click the panel's close control, and that the same menu item toggles it off again afterwards.
Verify the scene section matches the drawing: create exactly 2 elements and confirm the element count reads 2, and place two 100x100 rectangles side by side and confirm the width row reads about 200.
Verify the scene and total storage rows populate shortly after opening (they are computed with a 500 millisecond delay) and grow when you add elements.
Verify on a completely empty canvas the panel still opens cleanly, showing a count of 0 and zero or sensible width and height rather than NaN, Infinity, or an error.
Verify that with exactly one element selected the x, y, width, height and angle rows appear and match that element, and rotate it about 90 degrees to confirm the angle row reads roughly 90 degrees.
uncertainty: The exact wording of the new context-menu item is translation-driven and not supplied, so it must be located by its position in the canvas context menu; the selection-helper rename and the storage refactor appear purely mechanical in the diffs, so no specific old-versus-new regression input was identified and the highest-risk cases are edge inputs on the new panel itself.

report.summary: This release reworks the eraser keyboard handling in the Excalidraw drawing editor, changing how E and Escape switch tools in and out of eraser mode.
keyChanges: Pressing E to leave eraser mode now reactivates the tool that was active before erasing, falling back to Selection when no previous tool is recorded; previously it always returned to Selection.
Pressing Escape while the eraser is active now exits eraser mode through the same toggle, where previously Escape triggered the finalize action instead.

The finalize shortcuts (Escape to deselect or finish, Enter to finish a multi-point element) are unchanged whenever the eraser is not active, but their trigger condition was restructured and now explicitly excludes eraser mode, so a regression check is warranted.
qaChecks: Test: with a drawing tool other than Selection active, press E to start erasing, erase part of an element, then press E again; verify the tool you used before erasing becomes active again, whereas the old behavior always returned to Selection.

Check: with the eraser active but no previously used tool recorded, for example after switching to the eraser without pressing E first, press E and verify it falls back to the Selection tool and never leaves the editor stuck in eraser mode.

Verify: press E to activate the eraser, erase something, then press Escape; verify eraser mode ends and the previous tool (or Selection) becomes active, instead of the previous finalize behavior running while the eraser stayed on.
Check: press Escape in the middle of an erase drag and confirm eraser mode ends cleanly and the strokes already erased remain erased.

Ensure: with the eraser not active, Escape still deselects the current selection and still finishes an in-progress multi-point line, and Enter also finishes a multi-point line, exactly as before this change.
uncertainty: It is not established whether activating the eraser without the E key records the previously used tool; if it does not, exiting with E or Escape falls back to Selection rather than restoring the previous tool, so verify which fallback users actually see in that case.

report.summary: This release adds a custom-colors section with new Z through B keyboard shortcuts to Excalidraw's element stroke and background color pickers, reworks keyboard navigation inside those pickers, and leaves the canvas background picker default-palette-only.
keyChanges: Element stroke and background color pickers now show a separate custom-colors section listing up to 5 distinct colors that are not in the default palette, collected from non-deleted elements in the drawing with the most recently updated first, while the canvas background picker never shows this section.
Custom color swatches display their raw hex code as label and tooltip instead of a translated color name, and the picker's shortcut rows gain a new fourth row using the letters Z, X, C, V and B.

Keyboard navigation was reworked so arrow keys move within whichever section holds focus, Arrow Up and Arrow Down no longer jump while focus is in the custom-colors row, and letters beyond the default palette now focus the matching custom swatch.

The color pickers now receive the drawing's elements and app state so the custom list can be computed when a picker opens, while default palette colors and color application otherwise behave as before.

report.summary: This release adds a toggleable stats panel showing scene and selected-element measurements plus browser storage sizes, supported by internal refactors to selection helpers and storage-size calculation that should not change existing behavior.
keyChanges: The canvas context menu gains a new stats toggle that opens a panel showing the scene's element count, bounding width and height, and storage figures for the scene and total (formatted with unit suffixes such as b, k, M, G), plus position, size, and angle for selected elements: one element shows its own values and angle, several show a combined bounding box and count, and no selection shows no selection section.

The panel is off by default, its open/closed state is kept in browser storage across reloads but excluded from exported files, and clearing the canvas now preserves the panel's visibility instead of resetting it.
An internal selection helper was renamed and its callers updated, so the selection properties panel and the sharpness action should behave exactly as before.
The local-storage size calculation was refactored into a shared helper used for both the scene and total storage figures, so totals should be unchanged.
The debounced helper computing storage figures now supports cancellation and is cleaned up when the panel closes; other debounced behavior such as autosave is unchanged.
qaChecks: Verify the context menu shows the new stats entry, choosing it opens the panel with scene element count, scene width and height, and storage figures for scene and total, the panel can be closed, and neighboring entries such as the grid toggle still work.

Verify the selection display: with nothing selected no selected section appears, with exactly one element selected the panel shows that element's x, y, width, height, and angle in degrees, and with two or more selected it shows the selected count and a combined bounding box instead.
Verify storage formatting boundaries: an empty scene shows scene storage of 0 with the base unit, values below 1000 stay on the base unit, and a value at or above 1000 switches to the k-style suffix.
Verify the panel refreshes after edits: with the panel open, draw or delete a shape and the element count and storage figures update within about half a second.
Ensure that with the stats panel open, clearing the canvas keeps the panel visible and the element count drops to 0.
uncertainty: The on-screen label of the new stats menu entry and the expected display format for storage sizes were not supplied; values below 1000 render with a base-unit suffix (for example 999b) and 1000 or more switch to k, so confirm both match the intended design.

report.summary: This release reworks how the editor's properties panel determines the value it displays (preferring the element being edited, then the shared value of selected elements, then tool defaults) and rebuilds text creation and editing, so multi-selection property display and text flows need regression testing.
keyChanges: All property panel controls ("Stroke", "Background", "Fill", stroke width, sloppiness, "Opacity", "Font Size", "Font Family") now read through one helper that first prefers the element currently being edited (for example text in the inline editor), then the value shared by all selected elements (none when they differ), then a tool default.

Visible consequences: while text is being edited the panel now shows that text element's own properties, and a multi-selection with conflicting opacity now displays the default 100 where the previous build deliberately showed 0; a genuine 0% opacity also falls through to 100 because 0 counts as "no value".

Text creation now goes through a shared text-element factory that measures and centers text at creation, and submitting the inline text editor with no text no longer adds an empty text element to the drawing (the old build could leave one behind).
Double-clicking an existing text now edits that element in place, pre-filled with its current text, and on submit re-creates it with updated size and position only when the new text is non-empty.

Color pickers (element stroke, element background, and canvas background) now receive null instead of undefined when no common color exists; this is plumbing that should render the same but is worth one smoke check.
qaChecks: Verify that selecting two shapes with different opacities now shows 100 in the Opacity field (the old build showed 0) and that entering a new value applies to both shapes.

Verify that a shape set to 0% opacity still renders invisible on canvas after deselect and reselect and that the Opacity field does not silently display 100 for it; this is the most likely regression.
Verify that two shapes with different stroke colors show no preselected color in the "Stroke" picker and that picking a color applies it to both shapes.
Verify that clicking the canvas, typing text, and submitting places the text centered on the click point with a selection box that hugs the rendered text.
Verify that submitting the inline text editor with no text (for example pressing Enter while it is empty) adds no element, so nothing is selectable or draggable at that spot afterwards.
uncertainty: The new helper treats 0 as "no value", so both a conflicting multi-selection and a genuine 0% opacity now display the 100 default; showing 100 for conflicting selections may be intended (the code comments it as the default), but a real 0% element displaying 100 looks unintended and nothing documents the intended display, so the opacity-0 check above should settle it.

report.summary: Text inside shapes now reflows and recentres when font, size, or alignment changes and pasting styles affects bound text, and selection-based property changes may now include or exclude bound text, so testers should focus on container-bound text behaviour on the canvas.
keyChanges: Changing font size, font family, or text alignment on text bound to a container now rewraps the text to the container width (unless that text is being edited), vertically centres it, and can grow the container height to fit the text; previously the container was not resized this way.
Paste styles now triggers the same redraw for bound text, so copying style from one element and pasting onto a shape with bound text should reposition/reflow that text like a direct property change.

Property changes now determine the target set through the selection helper with bound text included for font size, font family, and text alignment, so changing these properties while a container is selected may also update its bound text; arrowhead, background, fill, opacity, sharpness, sloppiness, stroke, stroke style, stroke width still use selection without bound text.

The in-progress text editor style updater no longer grows the container while editing and instead records the container height as-is, so container sizing during live text editing may differ from before.
qaChecks: Test with the shape selected (not in text edit mode): change the font size to a much larger value and confirm the text rewraps within the container width, the container height grows if needed, and the text stays vertically centred inside the shape.
Test with the shape selected: change the font family and then the text alignment and confirm the text rewraps, recentres vertically, and does not overflow or detach from the shape.

Test while the text editor is open (editing the bound text) and change the font size or alignment from the panel: confirm the text does not get rewrapped mid-edit and the editing box does not jump or lose position.
Test pasting a style (for example font family or size) onto a shape with bound text: confirm the bound text reflows and recentres in the target shape the same way as changing the property directly.
Test pasting a style onto multiple selected shapes with bound text: confirm every target shape's text updates without overlap or clipping.
uncertainty: The graph shows property changes now route through a selection helper, but it is not proven for every property which exact selection scope (with or without bound text) each property ends up using; if container selection behaves inconsistently across properties, flag it with the property name and selection used.

report.summary: This release reworks how the Excalidraw eraser tool is exited: leaving the eraser now restores the tool used before it instead of always returning to selection, and Escape becomes a new way to switch the eraser off.
keyChanges: Pressing E while the eraser is active no longer always switches to the selection tool; it restores the tool that was active before the eraser was chosen, falling back to the selection tool only when no previous tool is recorded.
Escape now also exits the eraser when it is active and returns to the previously used tool; before this change Escape did not affect the eraser tool.
While the eraser is active, Escape no longer triggers the existing finish/cancel shortcut; that Escape and Enter behavior is unchanged whenever the eraser is not active.
qaChecks: Test the exact toggle that changed: select the rectangle tool, press E to switch to the eraser, erase something, then press E again — the editor must return to the rectangle tool, not to the selection tool as it did before this change.

Ensure repeated switching never strands the editor in the eraser: alternate between the eraser and drawing tools several times using E, confirming every exit lands on a usable drawing or selection tool (selection when no previous tool is recorded) and that the next E press always re-enters the eraser.
Check the new shortcut: with the eraser active, press Escape — the eraser must switch off and return to the tool used before the eraser (or the selection tool if none was recorded).

Verify both exit keys work from the same state: enter the eraser with E, exit with Escape, re-enter with E and exit with E, confirming each exit restores the previously used tool rather than triggering the old Escape behavior such as clearing the current selection.

Confirm existing shortcuts are unchanged while the eraser is not active: Escape still clears the selection of selected elements, and Escape or Enter still finishes a multi-point line or arrow being drawn.
uncertainty: Supplied evidence does not establish how the new previous-tool state is handled when editor state is stored or exported; nothing indicates a problem, but if saving and reopening right after using the eraser restores an unexpected tool, report it rather than assuming it is intended.

report.summary: This release changes how text bound inside shapes is handled during property updates: text properties now apply to that inner text with re-wrapping and container resizing, and property changes target a shared, explicitly filtered selection set.
keyChanges: Changing font size, font family, or text alignment now also updates text bound inside a selected shape; the text is re-wrapped to the shape's width, vertically re-centered, and the shape grows taller when the text no longer fits. Previously the inner text kept its existing line breaks and position and the shape's height was left untouched.
Pasting copied styles onto text bound inside a shape now uses the same re-wrapping, vertical centering, and shape-resizing behavior.

Property changes now derive their target set through a shared selection filter: text properties explicitly include bound text, while background, stroke, fill, opacity, sloppiness, sharpness, and arrowhead changes exclude it by default, and the selected-shape properties panel now also sees bound text as part of the selection.
While text inside a shape is being edited, the editor no longer enlarges the shape itself during a property change; shape sizing is handled by the redraw step instead.
qaChecks: Verify that selecting a shape containing text and increasing the font size in the properties panel also updates the text inside the shape.

Verify that with a long single line of text wider than the shape, increasing the font size re-wraps the text to fit the shape's width and the shape grows taller with the text vertically centered; the text must not keep its old unwrapped line breaks or overflow the shape.
Verify that changing font family and text alignment while the shape is selected likewise updates the inner text and leaves it wrapped and centered.

Verify that while editing text inside a shape, changing the font size updates the editing box in place without the text detaching from the shape, and after clicking away the text sits inside the shape, wrapped and vertically centered.

Verify that after making the text taller than the shape and then shrinking it again with a smaller font size or fewer lines, the shape settles at a sensible height instead of staying permanently enlarged.
uncertainty: The evidence does not establish whether non-text property changes previously also modified text bound to a selected shape, so it is unclear whether the inner text's color or opacity used to change together with the shape; use the previous release as the reference when judging those results.

report.summary: This release adds a canvas colors section to the element stroke and background color pickers, surfacing up to five recently used custom colors with new keyboard shortcuts, while the canvas background picker stays palette-only.
keyChanges: In the stroke and background color pickers, a new canvas colors section lists up to five distinct colors used in the current drawing that are not in the standard palette, ordered most recently edited first; deleted shapes are ignored and a repeated color appears once.

Those colors can be applied by clicking or with the new shortcuts Z, X, C, V, B for the first through fifth custom color, and arrow-key navigation now works within each section separately, with up and down arrows moving only within the standard palette.
The canvas background picker receives the same new data but shows no custom colors section, so its visible behavior should be unchanged.
Custom swatches show their hex code as label and tooltip together with the shortcut letter, and the section heading relies on a newly added translation.
qaChecks: Test the five-color cap: apply a sixth distinct custom color to a shape, reopen the picker, and verify only the five most recently used custom colors appear with the oldest no longer listed.
Verify the section excludes colors identical to standard palette swatches, lists a repeated custom color only once, and never lists the color of a deleted shape.
Verify clicking a listed canvas color applies it to the selected element's stroke or background as appropriate.
Verify pressing Z then X applies the first and second listed canvas colors respectively, matching the shortcut letters shown on the swatches.
Verify left and right arrow keys cycle through swatches within each section, including wrapping from the last swatch back to the first, and up and down arrows move within the standard palette.
uncertainty: The new shortcut handling appears to assume the canvas colors row exists: when it does not (always for the canvas background picker, or in element pickers before any custom color has been used), pressing Z, X, C, V or B may trigger an internal error with no visible reaction; this is the most likely regression in the release and is covered by the keyboard check above.

report.summary: A new distraction-free Zen Mode was added to the Excalidraw editor that hides toolbars and panels while drawing, toggled with the Alt+Z shortcut or a new footer button.
keyChanges: Pressing Alt and Z without Ctrl or Cmd now toggles a new distraction-free Zen Mode, which starts turned off in every fresh editor session.

While Zen Mode is on, the left toolbar and selected-shape panels, the bottom zoom controls, the lock tool, the footer language and shortcuts area, and the GitHub corner slide out of view and reappear when it is turned off.
The shortcuts dialog now lists a new Zen Mode toggle entry with the Alt+Z shortcut.

Styling changes to the shared toolbar button and the screen-edge container that holds the editor menus affect many toolbar buttons and dialogs, so all of those controls must still appear and work normally when Zen Mode is off.
The new Zen Mode setting is only added to the default editor state as off, so save, load, export, and clipboard copy behavior itself should be unchanged, but a quick regression check is prudent.
qaChecks: Verify pressing Alt and Z without Ctrl or Cmd hides the left toolbar panels, bottom zoom controls, lock tool, footer language and shortcuts area, and GitHub corner, and pressing the same keys again brings them all back.
Verify the exit Zen Mode button in the footer, which becomes visible only while Zen Mode is on, exits Zen Mode and restores every hidden panel.
Verify drawing and selecting shapes still work while Zen Mode is on, and that the toolbar and shape properties panels return correctly on exit.
Confirm Ctrl or Cmd plus Z still performs undo and does not toggle Zen Mode, since the shortcut only fires without that modifier.
Verify the shortcuts dialog shows a new Zen Mode entry with the shortcut Alt+Z and that pressing Alt and Z performs exactly that action as documented.
uncertainty: The footer exit button and shortcuts dialog entry rely on translated interface text, so in a language where the new Zen Mode wording has not been translated yet the button may show raw or missing text; check at least one non-English language.

report.summary: The release adds a keyboard-accessible section of colors already used in the drawing to the shape color pickers and reworks the picker's keyboard handling, making color picking across shapes and canvas the main regression surface.
keyChanges: Shape stroke and background color pickers gain a new section listing up to 5 colors from the drawing that are not in the default palette, ordered with the most recently updated shapes first; the canvas background picker deliberately never shows this section.

The custom swatches are clickable, apply their color when focused, and get new keyboard shortcuts Z, X, C, V, B alongside the existing 15 default-palette shortcuts; their tooltips and labels show the hex code instead of a color name.

Keyboard handling in the picker was rewritten: arrow keys now move only within the section that has focus, with the row-of-5 up/down jumps kept only for the default palette, so keyboard behavior in every color picker needs a regression pass.
All three picker popups (element stroke, element background, canvas background) were rewired to feed drawing data into the picker to enable the feature.

Highest-risk input: pressing Z, X, C, V, or B when no custom-colors section exists (a brand-new drawing, or the canvas background picker), because the shortcut now targets a section that is only rendered when custom colors are present.
qaChecks: Verify that with custom colors present, the picker shows a new section of colors taken from the drawing - at most 5 swatches, most recently updated shapes first - and that clicking or keyboard-focusing a swatch applies that color to the selected shape.

Test pressing Z, X, C, V, and B in the picker when the drawing has no custom (non-palette) colors, for example immediately after opening a new file: the picker should stay open and fully usable with no error, lost focus, or crash, since these keys now target a custom-colors section that does not exist in that case.
Confirm the canvas background picker never shows the custom-colors section, even in a drawing full of custom colors, and that it still changes the canvas background normally.
Validate the 5-swatch cap by applying 6 or more distinct non-palette colors to different shapes: exactly 5 custom swatches should appear, all taken from the most recently updated shapes.

Check arrow-key navigation with both sections visible: left and right arrows move within whichever section currently has focus and never jump across sections, and up and down arrows move in rows of 5 only within the default palette (within the custom section they stay in place).
uncertainty: On custom color swatches, the visibly shown shortcut letters (Z, X, C, V, B) may not match the shortcut announced to screen readers, which appears to still reference the first five default keys; verify with assistive technology if keyboard accessibility matters for this release.
