report.summary: The release adds a Zen mode to the whiteboard editor and rewrites toolbar button visibility handling, so the main QA focus is the new Alt+Z zen mode plus a regression pass over toolbar buttons and the standard editor layout.
keyChanges: A new Zen mode, off by default in every fresh session, is toggled with Alt+Z when Ctrl or Cmd is not held: it applies transition styling that is meant to slide the left toolbar, the selected-shape panel, the bottom zoom and encryption controls, and the footer language and shortcuts controls out of view, hides the lock icon and the GitHub corner, and adds a new exit-zen-mode button to the footer.

The keyboard shortcuts dialog now documents Alt+Z as the zen-mode toggle, and both the new footer button and this dialog entry depend on newly added interface labels that must resolve in every available language.

Toolbar button visibility was rewritten from an inline style into two CSS classes with a swapped mapping compared with before: previously a truthy or absent visible flag made a button visible and only an explicit false hid it, while now a truthy flag selects the hide class and a falsy one the show class, so any button driven by an explicit visibility flag, such as the one that finishes a multi-point line or arrow, may appear or disappear at the wrong moment.

The default editor state now carries the zen-mode flag through the save, load, share-link, export, and clipboard paths, and the fixed layout containers gained optional styling hooks, with no intended change to drawing content.
qaChecks: Verify pressing Alt+Z slides the left toolbar, the selected-shape panel, the bottom zoom and encryption controls, and the footer language and shortcuts controls out of view, hides the lock icon and the GitHub corner, and shows the new exit-zen-mode footer button, and that pressing Alt+Z again restores all of them.
Confirm the exit-zen-mode footer button is not visible while zen mode is off, becomes visible in zen mode, and clicking it returns the editor to the normal view.
Check that Ctrl+Alt+Z on Windows/Linux and Cmd+Alt+Z on Mac do not toggle zen mode, and that Alt+Shift+C still copies the canvas as a PNG image to the clipboard.

Validate that the keyboard shortcuts dialog, opened from the footer, lists Alt+Z for zen mode, and that after switching the interface language the zen-mode entry and the footer button still show readable labels rather than raw key names.

Test the finish button during multi-point drawing: click several times to draw a line or arrow without completing it, and verify the finish button stays visible and completes the shape when clicked, disappearing again once the shape is finished.
uncertainty: The stylesheet defining the new show and hide button classes was not part of the evidence, so it is unconfirmed whether those classes reproduce the previous visibility; if the class names mean what they say, buttons with an explicit visible flag would show and hide opposite to before, making the finish button during multi-point drawing the release's most likely regression.

report.summary: Excalidraw's canvas redraws are now throttled to the browser's animation frame rate with a trailing render of the latest state, so main-editor drawing updates, panning, and scrollbar behavior need regression testing.
keyChanges: The main editor now redraws the canvas through a new throttled renderer aligned to the browser's animation frame rate instead of redrawing synchronously on every state change.

Steps that previously ran immediately after each redraw — capturing scrollbars, detecting that the view scrolled outside the drawing, and scheduling image refresh — now run inside the throttled callback, so they can lag a state change by up to one frame and run once per redraw instead of once per update.

The frame throttle gained a trailing option used by the renderer: when several updates land within the same animation frame, at most one redraw runs immediately and the frame's latest state is applied in a following frame; previously only the first update in a frame was drawn and the final state could stay stale until the next update.

Canvas panning with wheel or space-drag, scrollbar dragging, and pointer-move handling still use the same frame throttle, whose flush and cancel internals changed, so interaction smoothness and end positions should be re-verified.
qaChecks: Verify that dragging a shape quickly and releasing it in one fast motion leaves the shape drawn at its final released position, since updates that previously landed within the same frame were skipped and could leave stale intermediate drawings.
Verify that creating, moving, and resizing several elements in rapid succession ends with all elements shown in their final state with no leftover intermediate frames.
Confirm that rapid successive edits keep the canvas responsive with no visible flicker, since each frame can now produce an immediate redraw plus one trailing redraw of the final state.
Verify that panning by mouse wheel or by holding space and dragging moves the view smoothly and stops exactly at the drag's end position without snapping back.
Verify that dragging an on-canvas scrollbar follows the pointer and settles at the release position with the scrollbars redrawn correctly afterwards.
uncertainty: The deferred post-render steps (scrollbar updates, scrolled-outside detection, image refresh) now execute asynchronously at the next animation frame and read the app state at that moment; the evidence does not establish whether fast scrolling while editing text or rapid bursts of state changes expose a visible timing glitch, so exploratory testing should cover those bursts.

report.summary: Canvas rendering in the Excalidraw editor is now throttled to one render per animation frame with a trailing re-render of the latest state, changing how drawing, dragging, panning, scrollbar visibility, and image refresh behave.
keyChanges: The main editor now renders the canvas through a new throttled path that executes at most once per animation frame; when several updates arrive within one frame, the latest state is re-rendered on a trailing frame so the final state is still drawn.

Steps that previously ran immediately after every render, such as scrollbar visibility, the app's scrolled-outside handling (which stays off while a text element is being edited), and image refresh scheduling, now run inside the throttled render's callback and can settle one frame later.

The shared animation-frame throttling utility was extended: a pending frame now uses the latest arguments at scheduling time instead of the first call's arguments, and callers can opt into a trailing re-run, which the new render path does.

A re-export of the canvas render function from the renderer package's index was removed, and the dependency graph shows no remaining users, so this appears to be cleanup with no intended behavior change.
qaChecks: Verify drawing several shapes with fast, continuous pointer drags (rectangles, lines, freehand strokes) leaves every shape fully rendered at its exact final position after release, with none missing or frozen at an intermediate position.
Verify rapidly dragging an existing element across the canvas and releasing places it exactly at the drop position, with its selection outline and handles still following during the drag.
Verify resizing and rotating a selected shape finishes with the final size and rotation displayed, and the canvas stays responsive throughout the gesture.
Verify holding the space key (or using pan mode) and dragging the canvas ends with the viewport exactly where released and all elements redrawn at correct positions.
Verify dragging the scrollbars moves the view and scrollbars appear and disappear correctly shortly after the drag ends, since scrollbar visibility now updates when the throttled render runs.
uncertainty: Scrollbar visibility, the scrolled-outside handling, and image refresh now run only when a throttled render frame actually executes, so they could lag one frame behind or be skipped for scene updates that do not trigger a render; confirm these still settle to the correct state after any scene change such as a drag, scroll, or image load.

report.summary: This release rebuilds how drawing libraries are imported and updated in Excalidraw through a single public update operation used by shared links, library files, and startup loading, changing the embeddable editor's public API and making library import and persistence the main QA focus.
keyChanges: Library imports were rebuilt around a single public update operation that replaces the old import API on the embeddable editor's public interface, so integrations that previously passed library items together with a scene update must now use two separate operations, which is a breaking change for host applications.

A shared library link, supplied in the page hash or the legacy query string, is now imported on page load and whenever the hash changes, prompting to confirm the number of shapes unless a matching token is present, merging the items as published, opening the library panel, and removing the link parameter from the address bar.

Opening or dropping a library file now merges its items into the existing library and opens the library panel automatically, while failed imports show an import error and canceled file pickers are treated as a silent abort.

On startup the editor now loads the saved library independently of the scene, and opening a scene no longer forces the library panel open or closed according to the panel state saved inside the scene file.
The embeddable package's example page was refactored from ref-based to callback-API usage, routing library files to the new update operation and displaying the pointer's x and y position on the page.
qaChecks: Verify that opening a link carrying a shared library address imports the library, shows a confirmation prompt naming the number of shapes, merges the shapes into an existing library, opens the library panel, and strips the link parameter from the address bar while leaving other parameters intact.

Check that declining the confirmation prompt leaves the library unchanged and produces no error dialog, since the previous release showed an import error in that case and the new flow rejects the update silently.
Verify that the legacy query-string form of the link also imports the library and removes the parameter from the address bar.
Ensure that changing the page hash to a library link during an open session imports the library without reinitializing the scene and restores the previous address afterward.
Verify that dropping a valid library file onto the canvas merges its items into the existing library and opens the library panel automatically.
uncertainty: The evidence shows that the library panel's import button now opens a file picker but does not show the step that imports the picked file into the library, so confirm that selecting a library file still imports it rather than merely opening the picker.

report.summary: This release adds a Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V plain-text paste mode and per-line text pasting, normalizes tabs and line endings in clipboard text and new text elements, and narrows the Shift+V vertical-flip shortcut, with spreadsheet-paste detection for tab-separated clipboard data as the highest regression risk.
keyChanges: A new plain-paste mode is available: pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V on the canvas pastes clipboard text as a single plain text element, skipping the spreadsheet chart dialog and rich-paste handling such as images, SVG, and previously copied drawings, while ordinary Ctrl/Cmd+V keeps the previous rich behaviour.

Ordinary pasting of multi-line text no longer creates one multi-line text element; it now creates one separate text element per line, trimming each line and collapsing consecutive blank lines into a single paragraph gap, and a one-time 5-second toast on desktop suggests the plain-paste shortcut.
Clipboard text and every newly created text element are normalized: tab characters become 8 spaces and Windows or Mac line endings become standard newlines.
The vertical-flip shortcut is narrowed: Shift+V still flips selected elements, but Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V no longer flips and now performs plain paste instead.

The shortcuts help dialog gains an entry for paste-as-plain-text, and pasting into an open text edit now always uses plain-paste behaviour, inserting raw text rather than offering chart or element handling.
qaChecks: Verify that after copying tab-separated rows from a spreadsheet application, a normal Ctrl/Cmd+V paste on the empty canvas still opens the chart-selection dialog and creates the expected chart.
Confirm that pasting the same spreadsheet content into an open text edit (double-click a text element first) inserts the rows as plain text lines without opening the chart dialog.

Verify that pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V with multi-line text copied from another application creates one single text element containing all the lines, with tabs rendered as spaces, and does not open the chart dialog.

Verify that ordinary Ctrl/Cmd+V of the same multi-line text creates separate text elements, one per line, with leading and trailing spaces trimmed and two consecutive blank lines collapsed to a single paragraph gap.

Verify the one-time toast suggesting the plain-paste shortcut appears after the first multi-line normal paste on desktop, lasts about 5 seconds, does not repeat on later pastes, and does not appear on mobile.
uncertainty: Clipboard text now has tab characters replaced with spaces before spreadsheet parsing, and spreadsheet detection splits rows on tab characters; pasting spreadsheet content copied from another application may therefore no longer be recognized as a spreadsheet and may not offer the chart dialog, so prioritize the spreadsheet-paste check above with real spreadsheet-copied content.

report.summary: Canvas drawing in the Excalidraw editor is now throttled to the animation framerate with the newest state always drawn last, so QA should confirm that rapid interactions still end on the correct final frame and post-render indicators stay accurate.
keyChanges: The editor canvas now redraws through a new render path capped at the animation framerate instead of redrawing synchronously on every update; when several updates arrive within one frame, the newest is queued and drawn in a follow-up frame so the final on-screen state should match the last action.

Post-render housekeeping - scrollbar tracking, the flag for the drawing being scrolled fully out of view, and scheduling image re-rendering for sharpness - moved into a completion step of the throttled render, so these can finish up to one animation frame later than before.

The shared frame-throttle utility gained an optional queue-the-latest-call mode used only by the render path; canvas panning, scrollbar dragging, and element dragging handlers use the utility without it and keep their previous timing.

Because the old code redrew synchronously and the new code relies on the queued follow-up frame, rapid bursts of scrolling, dragging, or zooming that end abruptly are the highest-risk inputs to verify.
qaChecks: Test a fast element drag: grab an element, drag it quickly across the canvas, and release abruptly; the element must be rendered exactly at the release position with no earlier intermediate position left on screen.
Test a rapid burst of scroll-wheel flicks to pan the viewport and stop abruptly; the canvas must settle showing the final viewport position, not an intermediate one.
Verify switching to another browser tab in the middle of an interaction and switching back: after returning, the canvas must show the correct current state.
Verify scrolling until no drawing content is visible still triggers the on-screen indication that the drawing has been scrolled away, and that scrolling back into view clears it.
Check the canvas scrollbars during and after a fast scroll burst; they must end up matching the final viewport position.
uncertainty: Post-render updates (scrollbar tracking, the scrolled-fully-out-of-view state, and image sharpening) now complete after the throttled frame rather than immediately; a visible delay of up to one animation frame may be intended behavior, and whether that lag is acceptable could not be resolved from the supplied evidence.

report.summary: This release reworks clipboard pasting: it adds a Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V paste-as-plaintext shortcut, splits multi-line text pastes into separate text elements, normalizes tabs and line endings in pasted and created text, and frees Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V from vertical flip.
keyChanges: A new paste-as-plaintext shortcut, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V, pastes clipboard text as a single element and skips chart-dialog and image detection; the help dialog now lists this shortcut, and a one-time toast on desktop hints at it after multi-line pastes.

Normal pasting of multi-line text changed: each non-empty line now becomes its own text element stacked with gaps, blank lines collapse to at most one paragraph gap, and lines are trimmed, whereas previously the whole text became one element.

Clipboard text and newly created text are now normalized before use: tab characters become spaces and Windows/Mac line endings become standard newlines, which affects rendering, measurement, and everything downstream that reads clipboard text.
Vertical flip no longer triggers on Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V (plain Shift+V is unchanged), because that key combination is now reserved for paste-as-plaintext.

Pasting while a text editor is open is now always treated as plain paste, so spreadsheet data and content copied from the drawing are inserted as text inside the editor instead of triggering the chart dialog or being dropped.
qaChecks: Verify pasting that multi-line text with Ctrl/Cmd+V creates one separate text element per non-empty line, stacked vertically with at most a single gap where the empty line was and each line trimmed, and that it no longer creates one element containing all lines.
Verify pasting the same content with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V creates exactly one text element containing every line, with the tab rendered as spaces.
Verify pasting clipboard content that contains only blank or whitespace-only lines adds nothing to the canvas.

Verify that after a multi-line Ctrl/Cmd+V paste on a desktop browser a toast appears once, telling the user they can paste as a single element with CtrlOrCmd+Shift+V, and that it does not reappear on subsequent multi-line pastes in the same session.
Verify pasting those tab-separated cells with Ctrl/Cmd+V still opens the chart dialog offering bar and line chart options, and that choosing an option inserts the expected chart.
uncertainty: Clipboard text is now normalized (tabs converted to spaces) before chart detection runs, so tab-separated cells copied from spreadsheet applications may no longer be recognized as a chart and the chart dialog may not appear on normal paste; the spreadsheet-paste check above decides this and it is the most likely regression in this release.

report.summary: Excalidraw rebuilt shared library links, library file imports, saved library persistence, and cross-tab sync to run through one library-update flow that merges imported shapes and opens the library panel automatically, and it replaced the old library-import interface used by embedded integrations.
keyChanges: All ways of loading a library, including shared library links carried in the page address or its legacy query-string form, library files, the first load from saved local data, and cross-tab sync, now run through a single library-update flow that can merge or replace, can ask for confirmation, and can open the library panel, and the shared-link handling moved into a shared handler that is now also exported to integrating developers.
Opening a valid .excalidrawlib file now merges its shapes into the existing library and automatically opens the library panel, which did not happen before.

The embedded editor's public interface changed: the old library-import call was removed and a new library-update call added, and passing library items through the scene-update call is now silently ignored, so existing host applications stop updating their library until they migrate.

When a shared library link points to a file that cannot be fetched or parsed, the previous release showed an import error message, but the new link-import path has no error-message wiring, so the failure is now silent while the library panel still opens.
The integration example app was migrated to the new library-update interface, including a new pointer-coordinate readout under its buttons.
qaChecks: Verify that opening the app through a shared library link with no token shows a confirmation dialog naming the number of shapes, and that accepting merges those shapes into the library, opens the library panel, and removes the link parameter from the address.
Confirm the legacy query-string form of the same link still imports the library on first load.

Verify that a shared library link pointing to a file that cannot be fetched or parsed surfaces an import error message; the old behavior showed one and the new path does not wire it, so record whether the failure is silent.

Check that changing the page address to a new shared library link while the app is already open imports the library once without duplicate shapes and restores the previous address without reloading the drawing.
Ensure that loading a valid .excalidrawlib file adds its shapes on top of the existing library without duplicating existing items and that the library panel opens automatically.
uncertainty: The evidence does not establish whether a shared library link present in the page address while the app is open is handled by exactly one of the two address-change handlers, so verify imported shapes are added exactly once, without duplicates, in that scenario.

report.summary: This release adds a paste-as-plain-text shortcut and changes multi-line text pasting to create one text element per line, with the highest risk that tab-separated spreadsheet pastes may no longer be detected for chart creation.
keyChanges: A new plain-paste mode lets users press CtrlOrCmd+Shift+V to paste clipboard content as one single text element, bypassing spreadsheet-chart detection and SVG/image import; the editor's help/shortcuts dialog now documents this shortcut.
The vertical-flip shortcut was narrowed so Shift+V alone still flips the selection, but CtrlOrCmd+Shift+V now triggers plain paste instead of flipping.

Clipboard and newly created text are now normalized (tabs become 8 spaces, Windows line endings become \n) before parsing; because this happens before spreadsheet detection, multi-column tab-separated pastes may no longer be recognized, and pasting while editing a text element now always uses plain-paste semantics.

report.summary: Library import and update behavior was reworked around one shared merge flow that opens the library panel, changing file, share-link, and persistence behavior and replacing the embeddable editor's public library command.
keyChanges: Opening or dropping a library file onto the canvas now merges its items with the existing library and automatically opens the library panel, which previously stayed closed on file import.

Library imports driven by the page address now run through one shared flow used by both the showcase app and the embeddable package: the hosted library is fetched, merged with the current items, saved as published, and the library panel opens, while the library parameter is removed from the address bar and mid-session address changes restore the previous address so the current scene link is preserved.

For embedding developers this is a breaking change: the editor's public command for importing a library was removed, scene updates can no longer carry library items, and a new library-update command plus shared link-import helpers were made available so hosts must wire the link behavior themselves.

At scene initialization the editor now forces the library panel to its current open or closed state instead of the state restored with the scene, and the showcase app now loads saved library items through the shared library flow instead of bundling them with the restored scene.
qaChecks: Verify dropping or opening a saved library file onto the canvas merges its items with the existing library without duplicating existing items and the library panel opens automatically.
Verify using the load control in the library panel imports a library file and its items become available to insert into the scene.
Verify importing a corrupt or invalid library file shows an import error message and keeps the existing library items unchanged.

Verify opening the app with the share-link parameter set to a hosted library address shows a confirmation listing the number of items to add; after confirming, the items appear in the library as published, the library panel opens, and the parameter disappears from the address bar.
Verify declining the confirmation leaves the library unchanged with no error message shown.
uncertainty: Third-party integrations that called the removed library import command or passed library items through scene updates will silently stop updating their library, and because no affected integration surfaces were supplied this migration risk can only be probed through the example page.

report.summary: This release rewrites how the editor measures text, removes a hidden per-text baseline value, redraws text on canvas with a simpler baseline, and adjusts text-box sizing and browser-specific quirks, affecting all text editing, resizing, aligning, and image or SVG exports.
keyChanges: Text sizing is now computed with a new width and height measurement engine instead of a hidden per-text baseline value, and old drawings or pasted content no longer carry that baseline, so re-opened or pasted text boxes may resize or reposition slightly differently than before.

Text attached to shapes or arrows, font changes, text alignment changes, font-size changes, and pasted styles all recompute through the new measurement path, so bound text should still fit and stay vertically aligned after those edits.

When resizing a single text box or a selection containing text, font size is now derived from the new width only, no longer from both width and height, so very small or large resizes may pick a slightly different font size than before.

On canvas the text is now drawn anchored to the bottom of each line and SVG export uses a simplified vertical offset, so exported images should match the canvas, but text that previously sat low inside a container may shift by a pixel or two.

The on-canvas text editor now sizes its box from measured text instead of counting browser lines, and on Firefox and Safari it widens the editor by half a pixel, reducing the known jumping-text problem on the first line of text inside a container.
qaChecks: Verify that typing a long single word into a text box inside a container still wraps at the container edge and does not overflow or jump, especially for the exact-width word case where the word fills the container width completely.

Verify that text copied from a word processor with Windows-style line endings (CRLF) pastes as normal multi-line text with the same box height as Unix-style line endings, since the new measurement normalizes line breaks.

Verify that editing the first line of text bound to a container, including deleting characters down to one line, does not jump vertically or double the container height; repeat on Firefox and Safari if available.
Confirm that re-editing an existing drawing saved before this release shows text at the same position and size, and that old drawings load and render without errors.
Verify that resizing a single text box scales the font size and that text still fits the new box width after resize, testing both growing and shrinking well below and above the original size.
uncertainty: Because the per-text baseline value is removed from the data model and text height is now approximated as font size times 1.2 instead of measured, drawings with unusual fonts or line spacing may shift slightly on reload or export; the exact visual delta for specific fonts is not established by the evidence, so spot-check hand-drawn-style fonts in particular.

report.summary: This release rewrites how text is measured, sized, wrapped, positioned, and rendered across the drawing editor and removes the stored text baseline, so all text behavior on the canvas and in exports needs retesting.
keyChanges: Text size is now calculated from the canvas plus an approximate line height of 1.2 times the font size instead of measuring rendered text in the browser, and the per-text baseline value that drove vertical positioning was removed from creation, file loading, binding, resizing, and rendering; multi-line text and the bundled hand-drawn fonts are most likely to shift.

For text bound to containers, resizing now derives the font size from width alone, and canvas and SVG rendering draw text with a bottom baseline without the previous bottom-alignment offset, so bottom-aligned and multi-line bound text can sit differently inside its container.

The inline text editor now sizes itself from measured text instead of counting rendered lines from scroll height, adds half a pixel of width on Firefox and Safari, and no longer clamps its width to the remaining viewport space.

Word wrapping changed at the edge case: a word exactly as wide as its container is now kept whole on its own line while still-wider words are broken character by character, and Windows-style line endings are normalized before measuring.

New standalone text no longer receives the small vertical offset derived from the removed baseline, so text placed with the text tool can sit slightly lower than before; older saved scenes still load because the obsolete baseline value is simply dropped.
qaChecks: Verify creating new text with the text tool: click an empty spot on the canvas, type two or three lines in the default font, and press Escape; the text stays where you clicked and the lines are evenly spaced without overlapping.
Check multi-line text typed in the hand-drawn font: line spacing looks even and the text box fully covers the drawn glyphs with no clipped tops or bottoms.

Validate pasting text containing Windows line breaks (copy a multi-line text or cell from an application like Notepad or Excel and paste it as a text element): each line renders on its own row and the box width matches the widest line.
Check editing an existing multi-line text element by double-clicking it and deleting lines down to one: the editing box shrinks smoothly and the single line stays vertically aligned without jumping.

Verify adding several lines of text inside a container and switching to the hand-drawn font: the text still fits inside the container without overflowing top or bottom and remains vertically centered or aligned as configured.
uncertainty: The new approximate line height of 1.2 times the font size may not match the real line height of every bundled font, which would make multi-line text boxes slightly shorter than the drawn glyphs occupy; whether any bundled font is actually affected could not be confirmed from the supplied evidence, and the container-fit and canvas-rendering checks above are intended to catch it.

report.summary: This release reworks how confirmation dialogs and menu selections behave across the Excalidraw editor.
keyChanges: The clear canvas confirmation now lives in a shared dialog component: choosing the clear canvas menu item opens a confirmation that stays visible even if the menu closes, and confirming still resets the drawing while canceling dismisses it.
Theme switching from the main menu no longer closes the menu when the theme toggles, letting users flip between light and dark repeatedly.
Menu items and links now support a shared selection handler, so embedded integrations can observe every menu selection without changing which menu item runs its own action.
The library menu's dropdown content now closes when any item inside it is selected, matching the behavior elsewhere.

report.summary: This release moves the clear-canvas confirmation dialog out of the main menu so it persists, and reworks menu-item selection so every editor or library menu closes on selection while the theme toggle intentionally keeps its menu open.
keyChanges: The clear-canvas menu item no longer keeps its confirmation dialog inside the main menu: a new app-level confirmation dialog shows the warning that the canvas will be cleared, so the dialog now survives the menu closing, which the previous version did not guarantee.

Menu items and menu links now run their own click handler first and then a shared, cancelable selection event; the main menu uses this event to close itself whenever an item is selected, unless the item cancels it.
The theme-toggle item cancels that selection event, so switching between light and dark themes deliberately keeps the menu open; it is the only item that does so.
The library menu's header dropdown now closes the library menu when any of its actions (import, export, publish, removal, reset) is selected; previously only clicking outside closed it.

uncertainty: How menu items closed the menu before this change is not fully visible in the evidence, so if a regular menu item now leaves the menu open or the theme toggle closes it, treat that as the most likely regression in this release.

report.summary: This release reworks how text is measured, positioned, wrapped, and resized across the drawing editor — replacing stored baseline values with approximate line-height math — so text in new drawings, reopened old files, container labels, and exports may render or scale slightly differently.
keyChanges: Text measurement was rewritten: line heights are now approximated at 1.2 times the font size, canvas text is drawn bottom-aligned per line, and the stored baseline value was removed from new text, saved files, and resizing, so vertical text positions and text box sizes can shift slightly in both new and reopened drawings.
Text wrapping changed for container-bound labels: a single word that exactly fills the container width is now kept whole on its own line instead of being broken character by character.
When resizing text or shapes with bound labels, the font size is now computed from width only; height no longer influences the resulting font size.

The in-place text editor for container-bound text now sets its height directly from the measured text instead of browser scroll height, and in Firefox and Safari the editor is rendered half a pixel wider with its width no longer clamped to the visible area.
Newly created standalone text no longer receives the previous vertical offset, so it appears directly at the click position.
qaChecks: Verify a newly created standalone text element appears with its first line centered on the exact point where you clicked or double-clicked, with no upward shift.
Verify multi-line text with at least three lines including one blank line renders with even line spacing on the canvas and nothing is clipped at the bottom of the text box.
Verify a text element placed near the right edge of the window opens its editing box fully inside the visible area when double-clicked.
Verify editing existing text by adding and deleting lines updates the text box size on the canvas to match the final text.
Check that a single long word sized to exactly fill the container width stays whole on its own line and is not split character by character.
uncertainty: The canvas now uses a bottom-aligned text baseline and an approximate line height of 1.2 times the font size instead of a measured baseline, so small vertical shifts in existing drawings are expected by design; the acceptable visual tolerance is not defined, so compare rendered output against a pre-change build for multi-line and bottom-aligned container text before sign-off.

Command palette coverage improved: the layer-order commands now also match searches like move up, move down, layer, and zindex, the line editor matches line, and bring-to-front now lists above bring-forward.

The Excalidraw+ sign-in entry in the main application menu and the 'Sign up' item on the welcome screen now show a login-style icon instead of the old arrow-to-bar icon; link destinations are unchanged.

Hardcoded pink badge styling was replaced with theme variables on the shape-toolbar promo badge, the 'Experimental' badge in AI/magic settings, the 'AI Beta' badge in the text-to-diagram dialog, and dropdown menu badges, so legibility now depends on theme colors.

report.summary: This release reworks how dropdown menu items report selection and moves the clear-canvas confirmation into a persistent shared dialog, making the destructive clear-canvas flow and menu open and close behavior the highest-risk areas to verify.
keyChanges: The clear-canvas confirmation is now rendered by a shared dialog outside the main menu, so it stays open after the menu is dismissed; confirming clears the canvas and closes the dialog, while canceling keeps the drawing intact.
Main-menu items now explicitly close the menu when selected, except the theme toggle, which intentionally keeps the menu open while switching between light and dark appearance.
The library menu header dropdown now closes automatically after an import, export, publish, remove, or reset action is chosen.

Menu items and link items now combine any existing click behavior with a new selection notification instead of overwriting it, and the main menu exposes a selection callback that embedded integrations can use.
qaChecks: Verify that selecting the canvas reset item in the main menu shows the confirmation dialog, closes the menu, and that the dialog remains visible after the menu is gone; previously the dialog disappeared together with the menu.
Confirm that accepting the dialog empties the canvas and closes the dialog.
Check that canceling the dialog closes it and all drawing elements remain untouched.
Verify that selecting a regular action such as load drawing, save, save as image, export, help, or live collaboration still performs the action and closes the menu.
Verify that clicking the theme toggle switches between light and dark appearance and leaves the menu open, which is the new intended behavior.
uncertainty: The new selection mechanism builds an internal selection event that is only passed to registered callbacks and the supplied changes show it is never fired into the page, so confirm that menu actions and menu closing still work even though no page-level selection event appears.

report.summary: This release redesigns the element layering controls with new icons and a swapped button order, adds a new line-editor button to the selection panel with changed availability and labels, improves command-palette search for layering and line commands, and moves several badges plus the sign-in icons from hardcoded pink styling to theme colors.

A new line-editor button appears in the selection panel when exactly one line or arrow is selected and no line-editing session is active, its label now differs for arrows versus other lines, and unlike before it is no longer offered while a line-editing session is open, where it previously served as the exit control.

The command palette now lists bring-to-front ahead of bring-forward, and new search keywords make the layering commands findable via move up, move down, zindex, and layer, and the line editor findable via line.

Badges switched from fixed pink styling to theme colors, so the small shape-toolbar badge, the Experimental badge in the AI settings panel, the AI Beta badge in the text-to-diagram dialog, and dropdown menu badges now follow the light and dark themes.
The Excalidraw+ sign-in link in the main menu and the Sign up item on the guest welcome screen now use a new login icon instead of the old arrow-to-left icon.

Verify with four stacked overlapping shapes that bring-to-front and send-to-back move the selected element all the way while bring-forward and send-backward move it one level.
Verify the redesigned arrow-style icons render clearly for all four buttons on desktop and in the mobile menu, with the send buttons visually distinguishable from the bring buttons.

report.summary: The sanitizer that makes URLs safe for HTML attributes now escapes ampersands, single and double quotes, and angle brackets instead of only double quotes, so QA should confirm that links and embedded content containing those characters still open and render correctly.
keyChanges: The shared HTML-attribute sanitizer used when writing element and embed URLs into attributes changed from escaping only double quotes to also escaping &, ', <, and >; it moved into the shared utilities module, and the related import edits change no behavior by themselves.

Link normalization feeds the element link editor, copy-element-link, link following, embedded content frames, SVG export, scene import and restore, and collaboration sync, so any link containing these characters is now transformed before it is written into an attribute.

URLs with query parameters containing & are the input most likely to behave differently: previously they passed through unchanged, and now they become & inside the attribute, which is only correct if every consumer decodes it back to &.
qaChecks: Check adding the link https://example.com/?a=1&b=2 (contains &) to an element: clicking the element must open the same URL with & in the browser address bar, not &; repeat once with a URL containing a double quote and a single quote.
Verify copying the element link to the clipboard yields the original URL unchanged when pasted.
Verify editing an existing link that contains & keeps the original characters after saving and reopening, and removing the link still works.
Verify inserting an embed URL with query parameters containing &, for example https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc&list=xyz, still loads and plays the embedded content inside the frame.
Confirm the embedded frame still points to the same destination after the scene is saved and reloaded.
uncertainty: The application context documents no before/after behavior for the sanitizer, and because links can be re-sanitized each time a saved scene or collaboration snapshot is loaded, double-escaping (for example &amp;) is the main unresolved risk; verify links containing & across repeated save and reload cycles and flag any visibly doubled escaping in the link editor or the opened URL.

report.summary: This release strengthens how link values are escaped before being placed into HTML attributes, so manual testing should focus on whether links and embedded content containing ampersands or other special characters still open, load, and export correctly.
keyChanges: Link values used across the editor are now escaped more aggressively before being placed into HTML attributes: previously only double quotes were escaped, and now ampersands, single quotes, and angle brackets are converted to HTML entities as well, so a URL such as https://example.com/?a=1&b=2 becomes one containing & in the prepared value.

This escaping applies wherever links are normalized or built: element hyperlinks and element links (via the link popup and link dialog), links handled when pasting, dropping, saving, loading, or copying, links for embedded website/video content on the canvas, and links written into exported SVG.

The only user-visible risk is that these escaped characters may reach places that do not decode them back, such as a link opened directly or an embedded page address; the remaining edits only relocate the escaping helper internally and add no separate behavior.
qaChecks: Verify that a shape given the link https://example.com/search?q=whiteboard&lang=en still shows and opens that exact URL, with both query parameters reaching the destination page rather than a parameter named amp;lang.
Check that links containing a single quote (for example https://example.com/?name=O'Brien) and a URL ending in an ampersand still open and pass their values through unchanged.
Verify that saving the drawing, reloading it, and reopening the link editor still shows a working URL that opens the original destination.

Verify that an embeddable created from a URL containing query parameters (for example a video link ending in &t=30) loads the correct content and honors those parameters, such as starting at the given time.
Confirm that after saving and reloading the drawing the embedded content still loads the same working address.
uncertainty: It is not established whether every consumer of these escaped link values decodes the HTML entities back to plain characters; if any flow uses the value raw, such as opening a link directly or loading an embedded page, URLs containing ampersands would break, so treat any live address containing & as the primary regression to confirm.

report.summary: This release strengthens how link and embed values are escaped when written into web pages and exported files, so normal URL behavior should be unchanged while drawings that use special characters in links deserve focused regression testing.
keyChanges: The helper that makes link values safe to place inside HTML and SVG attributes was moved to the shared utility layer and strengthened: it previously escaped only double quotes, and now also escapes ampersands, apostrophes, and angle brackets.

Every element hyperlink, embeddable web content, and copyable element link passes through this helper when created, edited, imported, or synced, so values containing those characters now reach the page as escaped attribute text that browsers decode back to the original characters in attribute contexts.
SVG export is the main intended beneficiary: exported drawings whose links contain ampersands or angle brackets should now produce valid files where they could previously come out malformed.

The main regression risk is any place that treats the value as plain text instead of an attribute, where the extra escaping can surface literally, most visibly an ampersand typed by the user appearing as its escaped form in copied or displayed links.
qaChecks: Check a link containing an ampersand: save it on an element, reopen the link editor, confirm the field still shows the URL exactly as typed, then follow the link and confirm the target page opens with every query parameter intact rather than a merged ampersand-parameter.
Check a link containing an apostrophe and one containing angle brackets: saving, redisplaying, editing, and following should behave exactly as before this change.
Confirm removing the link still clears it and the element reopens with no link.
Test an embeddable link whose address contains an ampersand between parameters: the embedded content should load and behave exactly as before, with all parameters applied.
Confirm the embedded content still displays on the canvas after saving, closing, and reopening the drawing.
uncertainty: The evidence shows which helpers apply the new escaping but not whether every consumer uses the escaped value strictly as an HTML or SVG attribute; if any surface passes it on as plain text, such as a copied link or the link editing field, users would see the extra escaping literally, so treat any literal escaped characters in displayed or copied links as a regression and note which action produced them.

report.summary: The canvas eraser tool was rebuilt internally with the same visible trail and Alt-restore behavior, so core erasing, group handling, and edge cases need retesting on the editor drawing canvas.
keyChanges: The eraser tool now finds elements to erase with a new dedicated eraser component that compares the eraser stroke against element outlines using the existing zoom-based hit threshold, replacing the previous approach of sampling points along the stroke, so results at element edges and on very fast strokes may differ.
Holding Alt while erasing still restores previously marked elements, now handled inside the eraser component, with whole groups, shapes with attached text, and their containers restored atomically.
The eraser trail visuals (size 5, smoothing, fade timing, and light/dark theme colors) were carried over unchanged, but the trail now renders above the lasso trail in the layer order.
The previous eraser explicitly skipped locked elements; the rebuilt eraser logic shows no equivalent skip, so locked elements may now be marked for erasure.
qaChecks: Check: drag the eraser across a line and a rectangle; each crossed element should highlight as pending erasure during the drag and be removed when the pointer is released.
Verify: the fading eraser trail still follows the pointer while erasing in both the light and the dark theme, since its size, smoothing, and fade timing were carried over.
Test: finish one eraser stroke and start a second one elsewhere; the second stroke should only affect newly crossed elements, because the pending-erasure list resets at the start of each stroke.
Test: erase across elements so they are marked for erasure, then hold Alt and drag back over them; they should return to normal while the eraser is still active.
Ensure: with Alt held, dragging over a shape that has attached text restores both the shape and its text together.
uncertainty: The rebuilt eraser iterates the elements it considers visible and contains no explicit skip for locked elements, which the previous implementation had; whether locked elements are actually covered depends on that visible set, so treat a locked element becoming erasable as a regression and confirm with the team whether it is intended.

report.summary: This release rewrites how the Excalidraw eraser decides which drawing elements to erase, moving detection into a new eraser-trail component with segment-based hit testing, so the eraser tool on the canvas is the main thing to regression-test, especially locked elements and fast strokes.
keyChanges: The eraser tool now detects what to erase by testing the eraser stroke as a line segment against each visible element (plus a point-inside check for filled shapes) in a new eraser-trail component, replacing the old approach of sampling individual points along the stroke; the trail's visual settings (size, smoothing, fade timing, theme-based color) were carried over unchanged.
Holding Alt while erasing now only restores elements that are already marked for erasure, and groups plus text attached to a shape are still marked and restored as a unit.

The old eraser logic explicitly skipped locked elements while erasing; the new logic contains no locked-element check, so locked shapes may now be marked for erasure, which is the highest-risk behavior change.
Starting a new eraser stroke now clears the previous stroke's marked elements and cached hit-test data, and the eraser trail overlay is now drawn after (on top of) the lasso trail overlay.
qaChecks: Verify slowly dragging the eraser across a filled rectangle marks it for erasure as soon as the stroke crosses it and removes it when the pointer is released.

Test dragging the eraser very quickly across several thin lines in a single stroke and confirm every crossed line is marked and erased, since fast strokes exercise the new segment-based detection differently from the old point sampling.
Ensure erasing over elements fades them, then holding Alt and dragging back over those same elements un-fades and restores them before release.
Check dragging the eraser across a locked shape and confirm the locked shape stays visible and is not marked for erasure or removed on release.
Confirm unlocked shapes crossed during the same eraser stroke are still marked and erased normally.
uncertainty: The previous eraser code skipped locked elements while the rewritten eraser logic contains no such skip, so whether locked shapes can now be marked for erasure is not settled by the evidence; the locked-element check above is the decision point, and if a locked shape fades or is deleted, treat it as a regression.

report.summary: The eraser tool's internals were rewritten behind an unchanged canvas workflow, so manual QA should focus on erasing and restoring accuracy, locked elements, and eraser trail visuals.
keyChanges: The eraser tool was re-implemented: during an erase drag, detection now compares the line segment between the last two trail points against element outlines using a tolerance that scales with zoom (and treats the cursor ending inside a shape as a hit), replacing the previous sampling of points along the drag path; drag-to-erase with deletion on release should look the same to users.
Erasing a whole group atomically, removing text attached to an erased shape, and holding Alt to drag back over already-marked elements and restore them are all preserved by the new logic.
The old rule that skipped locked elements while erasing no longer appears in the new logic, so locked elements may now be marked for erasure and deleted on release; this is the main regression risk.

The eraser trail keeps its previous look (size 5, fading tail, translucent dark in light theme and translucent light in dark theme) but is now drawn as the topmost trail layer above the lasso trail, and trail and pending-erasure state now reset when each stroke starts and ends.
qaChecks: Test dragging the eraser across standalone shapes and releasing: touched shapes should be marked for erasure during the drag and actually deleted from the drawing after release.

uncertainty: The rewritten erase logic shows no replacement for the old check that excluded locked elements from erasure, and the supplied evidence does not show whether a later step still protects locked elements; treat the locked-element check as the release's highest-signal test and flag any locked element that gets erased or highlighted for erasure.

report.summary: Excalidraw adds three crowfoot arrowheads and redesigns the arrowhead picker with remapped shortcuts and new keyboard navigation, so arrow styling, picker interaction, and arrow export need focused re-testing.
keyChanges: Arrows now support three new crowfoot arrowheads (one, many, and one-or-many) on both start and end heads, drawn with a larger head size (20 versus 15 default and 12 for diamond) and new geometry that also feeds selection bounds and hit testing.

The arrowhead picker now shows every head option, several of which were previously hidden, with only 4 always visible and the remaining 7 under a collapsible More options section that expands automatically whenever the selected head is hidden.

Arrowhead shortcuts were remapped: e now applies triangle (was bar), r applies triangle outline (was circle), triangle moved from t to e, circle from r to a, bar is now z, and d, f, s, c, x, and v newly cover diamond, diamond outline, circle outline, and the three crowfoot heads.

Picker keyboard navigation changed: Up and Down move a full row of 4 options, Left and Right move one option, and Tab now cycles through option values instead of closing the picker, while Escape and Enter still close it.
Crowfoot heads flow through the same rendering path used for SVG export, so exported diagrams must match the on-canvas crowfoot appearance.

report.summary: This release adds three crowfoot arrowhead styles to Excalidraw arrows and reorganizes the arrowhead picker, changing which styles are visible, their keyboard shortcuts, and in-picker keyboard navigation.
keyChanges: Arrows gain three new crowfoot end styles (one, many, and one-or-many) with dedicated icons; many and one-or-many draw two prongs and one-or-many adds a single crossbar, and these styles use a larger selection size of 20 versus 15 for other styles.

report.summary: Single-record reads now support an _embed option to include related items, and because the new embed step runs for every found record, even plain single-record responses need regression testing.
keyChanges: Requesting one record of a collection by its id now accepts an _embed query parameter: when the record is found, the service looks up the related collection named by _embed and attaches the items that reference that record, matching a field named after the parent collection plus 'Id' against the record id; before this change _embed was ignored and the bare record was returned.

The new code does not check whether _embed was provided, so the embed lookup now runs on every successful single-record read: a missing value is wrapped and then used both as the related-collection name and as the field name written onto the returned record.

Embed results are assigned to a single field named after the entire _embed value rather than once per requested value, so a request with several _embed values produces at most one combined field instead of one field per collection.
qaChecks: Verify that reading an existing record with no _embed parameter (and also with an empty _embed= value) returns the record body unchanged compared with the previous release, with no added field, empty-named property, or error, since the embed step now executes even when no related collection is requested.

Verify that reading the same record with _embed set to a related collection name returns the record together with that collection's items filtered to those whose parent-collection-plus-'Id' field equals the record id, under a field name matching the requested value.
Verify that reading a nonexistent record id still returns the empty not-found response.

Verify that a single-record read with two _embed values (the parameter repeated for two different related collections) returns each requested collection in a way consumers can identify; the implementation writes embed results under one field name built from the entire _embed value, so confirm the actual response shape and that no requested collection is silently lost.
uncertainty: The available evidence does not show what the underlying data lookup returns when given the wrapped missing value used for requests without _embed, so the exact outcome of a plain single-record read (unchanged body, an added empty-named field, or a failed request) is unconfirmed; record the actual response for that case.

report.summary: This release switches the server's data file saving from synchronous to asynchronous, making write-to-disk timing after API changes the main QA risk.
keyChanges: When the server is started with a database file, it now saves writes to that file in the background instead of completing each save during the request, so create, update, and delete responses can be sent before the file on disk is updated.
Until the background save finishes, a confirmed change exists only in the running server's memory and could be lost if the process stops abruptly.

The server's startup path and its data-handling helpers all receive the now asynchronously backed database object, so every read or write path is exposed to this timing change even though static analysis found no direct dependents of the edit.
qaChecks: Verify that creating one item through the API, immediately stopping the server, and restarting it leaves that item present both in the served data and in the data file on disk; the immediate stop right after the write is the key condition because saving is now asynchronous.
Check that several create and update requests sent in rapid succession all appear in the data file after the server is stopped and restarted, with each item holding the value from its last request.
Verify that deleting an item and restarting the server leaves it absent from the data file.

Confirm the server starts without errors against the existing data file and serves the pre-existing records unchanged.
uncertainty: It is not confirmed from the change whether every write path waits for the background save before sending its response, so a change acknowledged by the API may briefly exist only in memory; no pages, routes, or documented behaviours were supplied for this repository, so the exact client surfaces could not be named.

report.summary: Single-record API reads gain an embed option that attaches related records, but the new embed logic also runs on plain and multi-collection requests, so both the new feature and existing single-record responses need testing.

report.summary: This release adds related-record embedding to the single-record read API through a new _embed query parameter, and every single-record request now passes through new processing that previously ignored that parameter.
keyChanges: A request for one record now accepts an _embed query parameter and, when the record exists, attaches related records whose parent-id field matches the requested record id, whereas previously any _embed value was silently ignored and the bare record was returned.

The new code turns _embed into a list and loops over it but always writes a single property named from the whole list, so requests with two or more _embed values may return one combined field or nothing useful instead of separate embedded lists.

Because the new branching runs on every single-record read, requests sent without _embed, with an empty _embed value, or with an embed name matching no collection now take code paths that previously returned the bare record unchanged, so these inputs are where regressions are most likely to appear.
qaChecks: Verify a single-record request without any _embed parameter returns exactly the record as before the change, with no error and no unexpected added field.
Check a request with one _embed value returns the record together with that related collection filtered to the records whose parent-id field matches the requested record id.
Confirm a request carrying two _embed values in one URL returns both related collections as separate embedded fields rather than a server error, an empty response, or one combined field.
Ensure a request with an empty _embed value returns the record as before the change, without an error or a stray empty-named field, since that input was previously ignored.

Ensure a request whose _embed value matches no collection in the data store returns a handled response, such as the plain record or a clear client error, rather than a server crash, because such values were ignored before the change.
uncertainty: The new embedding loop never uses the individual value it iterates over and instead names a single property from the whole list each pass, so multi-value requests are the most likely regression; the supplied context documents no intended output for several _embed values, so confirm the expected response shape with the team if that check fails.

report.summary: The request helper now supports instances with built-in default options while existing request behavior should stay unchanged, so QA focuses on default-option merging plus regression checks on plain requests and error handling.
keyChanges: The HTTP request helper in ofetch gained a create method that builds a derived request instance carrying default options: per-request options override the instance defaults, instance defaults override anything inherited from the parent instance, and calling create with no arguments keeps the parent's defaults.

Requests made without any defaults follow the same path as before except the helper now passes a shallow copy of the caller's options instead of the caller's object itself, so it no longer rewrites the options you pass (for example by stringifying the body in place).

Header construction and the underlying request call now use the fetch and Headers implementations supplied to the helper, which keeps non-browser Node-based entry points on their own environment's implementations.
No application pages, flows, or roles were supplied for this repository, so verification happens wherever outgoing HTTP requests are issued rather than on a screen.

Test calling create with no arguments: the returned instance should work normally, inherit the parent's defaults, and send requests without errors.
Verify a plain request with a JSON object body and no explicit content-type still arrives as a stringified body with content-type application/json.

Test reusing one options object across two consecutive requests, which is input this change now treats differently: both requests should send the intended body and headers because the helper copies options instead of editing the object you pass.
Verify a request that fails (unreachable address or error status) still surfaces the error to the caller and invokes the request-error callback as before.
uncertainty: No application context, pages, or flows exist for this repository, so navigation and business ownership of these request paths could not be established, and no documented pre-change rules were available to compare the new default-merge semantics against.

report.summary: The ofetch HTTP client adds a create() method for building instances with reusable default request options, and requests now use the fetch implementation and Headers class supplied when an instance is built instead of the environment globals.
keyChanges: A new create() method on the package's fetch client builds a separate instance whose default request options apply to every request it makes: defaults supplied at creation merge with any parent defaults, and options passed on an individual request override those defaults for that request, with the merge done at the top level so a per-request value replaces a default of the same option name.
This is new behavior: previously, supplying defaults when building an instance had no effect because the request executor applied only the options given per call.

The actual network call and the construction of headers for JSON bodies now go through the fetch implementation and Headers class supplied at instance creation; previously the environment's global fetch and global Headers were used even when an implementation was injected, which the package's Node and undici variants rely on.
Instances built without any defaults behave as before, so existing consumers that pass only per-request options are not expected to see a change.

Confirm a request-level headers object replaces an instance default headers object wholesale rather than merging with it, and record whether consuming code expects both sets to apply.

uncertainty: The context documents no intended merge depth for nested default options such as headers: the new merge is shallow, so a request-level headers object fully replaces an instance default headers object instead of extending it, and whether that matches consumer expectations was not documented.

report.summary: This release lets callers derive fetch instances that apply shared default options to every request, changing how options, headers, and JSON body handling resolve when defaults are set.
keyChanges: The public fetch helper gains a create() method that returns a new instance applying the supplied default options to every request, while the original instance stays unchanged.

Because defaults are now merged before payload handling, an instance created with a default payload method such as POST serializes a plain-object body as JSON with an application/json content type even when the call omits the method.
Defaults can stack: deriving a new instance from an already-derived one applies both layers of defaults to every request.

report.summary: The shared HTTP client now decides how to parse each response body from the response content type instead of always reading it as text, with a per-request format override, and since no application screens were supplied QA must verify this at the library level.
keyChanges: Response bodies are no longer always read as text and run through the smart JSON parser: responses with an application/json or application/ld+json header, or with no content type at all, still parse as JSON exactly as before, types such as application/xml, application/html, image/svg, or any type starting with text/ return the raw text, and any other type such as application/octet-stream or image/png now returns a Blob.

A new per-request setting lets callers explicitly choose JSON, plain text, Blob, or raw binary parsing instead of relying on the content type, while a custom body-parsing callback still takes precedence and continues to receive the raw text as before.

Visible consequences for existing callers: binary or unrecognized content types now yield a Blob instead of a decoded string, and text-typed bodies skip the smart parser, so values like 123 or true stay strings instead of being coerced to number or boolean.
Error responses are parsed by the same new content-type rules before error handling runs, so non-JSON error bodies now arrive as text or Blob rather than always as smart-parsed values.
qaChecks: Verify a small binary response with a content type such as application/octet-stream or image/png arrives on the response data as a Blob (previously it came back as a decoded text string), and confirm nothing downstream still treats that data as a string.

Check a text/plain response keeps raw-text semantics: a body of 123 must return the string '123' (the previous parser coerced it to the number 123), and a JSON document served with a text/plain header must return an unparsed string rather than a parsed object.

Validate the JSON baseline is intact: application/json and application/ld+json responses with or without a charset suffix, and responses with no content type header, must still return the parsed object exactly as before.

Test one JSON endpoint requested three times with the format forced to plain text, Blob, and raw binary buffer and confirm the returned data is a string, a Blob, and an ArrayBuffer respectively, regardless of the response content type.
Confirm forcing the JSON format makes even a non-JSON header parse as JSON, for example a text/plain body of 123 must return the number 123 when JSON is requested explicitly.
uncertainty: No downstream consumers, pages, or screens are mapped, so QA cannot confirm who relies on the old always-text behavior; one concrete edge is that an SVG served with its standard image/svg+xml header is not matched by the text-type list (only the exact token image/svg is) and now returns a Blob, so verify whether any consumer fetches SVG expecting text.

report.summary: The shared fetch client now picks how each response body is parsed based on the response Content-Type header or an explicitly requested format, instead of always reading the body as text and smart-parsing it, which changes the data type callers receive for non-JSON responses.
keyChanges: Response bodies are no longer always read as text and passed through the built-in smart parser; the client now chooses a parser from the Content-Type header — JSON for application/json and application/ld+json (ignoring parameters such as charset), plain text for any text/ type plus XML, XHTML, HTML and SVG, and a Blob or ArrayBuffer for everything else, while a response with no Content-Type header still follows the JSON path.

Callers can now explicitly request a response format — text, a binary Blob, an ArrayBuffer, or JSON — overriding header detection, while a custom parsing option still takes precedence and forces JSON-style text parsing as before.

Because smart parsing no longer runs on every body, some inputs change shape: text responses whose bodies look like values (for example 123 or true) now arrive as the strings "123" and "true" instead of the number 123 and boolean true, and JSON payloads served under other +json vendor content types are no longer parsed into objects.

report.summary: This release changes how the HTTP client interprets response bodies, choosing a parser from the server's content type or a new caller option instead of always reading the body as text and leniently parsing it as JSON.
keyChanges: Previously every response body was read as text and leniently parsed as JSON; now JSON content types ('application/json', 'application/ld+json') and responses with a missing content type keep that lenient parse, text-like types ('text/*', 'application/xml', 'application/xhtml', 'application/html') return the raw string without parsing, and every other type returns a downloadable binary file (Blob).

A new option lets callers force the response to be handled as plain text, a binary file, raw bytes, or JSON, while a caller-provided custom parser still takes priority and keeps the old read-as-text-and-parse behavior.

As a result, a plain-text body like '42' now stays the string '42' instead of becoming the number 42, binary downloads come back as usable files instead of garbled strings, and suffixed JSON types such as 'application/problem+json' are no longer recognized as JSON and now return files, which is the most likely regression.
qaChecks: Verify a response with 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' still returns a parsed object, including for a numeric body such as 42.

Test an endpoint returning 'Content-Type: application/problem+json' with a JSON error body and confirm its fields are still readable as a parsed object; if the result arrives as an opaque binary file instead, report it as a regression introduced by this change.

Check a 'Content-Type: text/plain' response with body '42' returns the string '42' and that consumers comparing or computing with it still work with a string, since it previously became the number 42.
Confirm 'application/xml' and 'text/html' responses return the raw markup string rather than a binary file.
Test downloading a file served as 'application/pdf' or 'image/png' and confirm the returned data is a usable binary file (Blob) that can be saved or previewed, not a garbled string as before.
uncertainty: The new JSON detection only matches 'application/json' and 'application/ld+json', so standard suffixed JSON types such as 'application/problem+json', 'application/hal+json', or 'application/vnd.api+json' now return binary files where the previous release parsed them as JSON; whether consuming integrations actually serve these types is unknown, so treat any file-instead-of-JSON result as confirmed impact.

report.summary: The library now computes extension detection, parent-folder extraction, relative paths, path building, and the full file-name breakdown with its own logic instead of delegating to Node's built-in path module, so edge inputs such as hidden dotfiles, bare file names, relative paths, and root-anchored requests can now produce different results and need focused regression testing at the library API level.
keyChanges: Hidden files such as '.gitignore' used to report no extension because their only dot is the leading character; the rewritten extension logic now reports '.gitignore' as the extension, and the full file-name breakdown inherits this, showing a hidden file with an empty name and the whole name as the extension.

The full file-name breakdown also changed for relative and bare paths: parsing 'reports/june.csv' now reports the root as 'reports' on top of the folder (the root used to be empty), so rebuilding a path from the parts can duplicate the folder, and parsing a bare name like 'notes.md' now reports the root as the file name itself and the folder as '/'.
Parent-folder extraction was rewritten, so a bare file name like 'README.md' now yields '/' as its folder where it used to yield '.'.

Path building from parts now assembles root, folder, and file (or name plus extension) itself: a folder part ending with a slash such as 'uploads/' can produce a doubled slash ('uploads//a.png'), and combining a root with a relative folder now anchors the result at the root ('/uploads/a.png' instead of 'uploads/a.png').

Relative-path calculation is now a common-prefix trim after resolving both sides, so from '/' to '/data' the answer can be '../data' where it used to be 'data', and from a file to its own folder the answer is '..' without the trailing slash Node produced.
qaChecks: Check the extension reported for a hidden file with no other dot, such as '.gitignore': it used to come back empty and now comes back as '.gitignore'; confirm downstream extension filtering and file-type display still behave sensibly for hidden files.
Validate the full breakdown of '.gitignore': the name part is now empty and the extension part holds the whole name, where it used to be name '.gitignore' with no extension.

Verify a build-from-parts round trip of a relative path such as 'reports/june.csv' still produces exactly 'reports/june.csv'; the parts now also carry the root 'reports', so a rebuild can come back as 'reports/reports/june.csv' or as an absolute path.

Test the full breakdown of a bare name such as 'notes.md': the folder part is now '/' and the root part is the file name itself, where it used to be '.' and empty; confirm nothing downstream treats '/' as a real containing folder.
Confirm the folder of a bare file name such as 'README.md': it is now '/' where it used to be '.'; verify any join or comparison that relied on '.' still resolves to the same location.
uncertainty: It is not documented whether the new edge-case results — hidden files reporting an extension, '/' instead of '.' for bare names, a populated root for relative paths in the breakdown, root anchoring in the path builder, and leading '..' from the root in relative paths — are intended rewrites or accidental deviations from the Node-compatible behavior this library previously delegated to; confirm intent with the team before signing off.

report.summary: This release swaps the Node built-in path engine for the library's own in-house implementations across its path utilities, changing several edge-case results for file breakdown, extension handling, folder lookup, relative paths, and path building that downstream consumers should verify.
keyChanges: Full path breakdown is reimplemented and now diverges on several inputs: relative paths put the first directory segment (or the whole bare filename) into the root part instead of leaving it empty, trailing-slash paths lose the filename part, and dotfile names are split as extensions so the name part comes out empty.

Extension lookup now reports an extension for dotfiles such as '.bashrc' where the previous engine returned none, and stripping an explicitly empty extension now returns an empty filename instead of the full one.
Relative-path calculation from the filesystem root to a first-level absolute path now includes an extra up-level step, returning '../a' instead of 'a' for root to '/a'.
Directory lookup for a bare filename or an empty input now returns the root slash instead of the previous single dot.

Path building now resolves root-ful results through internal resolution and concatenates the name and extension parts literally, so a missing name or extension can surface the literal text 'undefined' inside built filenames that previously came out clean.
