Check the bare filename 'notes.txt': the root part should stay empty (not 'notes.txt') and the directory part should be '.' (not '/').
Check the trailing-slash path 'assets/images/': the filename should still be 'images' with directory 'assets', not an empty filename.
Check the dotfile '.bashrc': the extension should remain empty and the name should stay '.bashrc', not an extension of '.bashrc' with an empty name.
Check extension lookup on the dotfile '.bashrc': it should return an empty extension as before, not '.bashrc'.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not state whether exact parity with the previous engine is required; since this library is a drop-in replacement for the Node built-in path module, treat every divergence above as a regression candidate until the team confirms, with the stray 'undefined' text in built paths and the extra up-level step for root-relative paths the most likely user-visible breaks.

report.summary: The URL-utility library's core was rebuilt around a new URL object, changing how URLs are joined, how repeated and special query parameters behave, and which inputs are accepted; no pages, routes, or roles were supplied, so verification is at the library level.
keyChanges: URL joining now throws a controlled 'Cannot append a URL with protocol' error when any segment after the base contains a protocol, where it previously merged such URLs, and a later segment's fragment now replaces the base's fragment instead of being dropped.

Repeated query parameters are preserved instead of collapsed: reading parameters from '?tag=a&tag=b' now returns both values as a list (previously only the last value), so re-applying parameters keeps all occurrences where the old behavior reduced the URL to '?tag=b'.

Input acceptance narrowed: passing anything other than a string to URL creation now raises a type error (a pre-parsed URL object was previously accepted), and the normalize helper no longer honors the removed strip-base flag, so callers asking for a stripped path now receive the full URL.

Query and URL text encoding changed: spaces in parameter names serialize as '+' (literal '+' becomes %2B), and characters such as [ ] | in paths and { } ^ in hashes are emitted raw instead of percent-encoded, altering the exact URL text produced.
Slash handling is now centralized: joins place exactly one slash between segments, and double-slash cleaning collapses repeated slashes everywhere except right after a scheme, preserving '://'.
qaChecks: Verify that joining with a protocol-bearing segment (base 'http://a.com/start' plus 'http://b.com/page') raises the controlled 'Cannot append a URL with protocol' error instead of silently merging the two URLs as it used to.

Verify that plain path joining yields exactly one slash between segments and keeps a final trailing slash (base 'http://h/a/' plus 'b/' gives 'http://h/a/b/'), that a later segment's query parameter overrides a same-named base parameter, and that a later segment's fragment now replaces the base's fragment (previously the base's fragment was kept).
Verify that joining an empty segment leaves the base URL completely unchanged.

Verify that a URL with the same parameter twice (for example '?tag=a&tag=b') keeps both values when parameters are re-applied, where the old behavior collapsed it to the last value ('?tag=b'), and that reading parameters back returns both values as a list rather than a single string.

Verify that a parameter name containing a space (the way a label copied from another tool might arrive) serializes with '+' in place of the space (for example '?my+key=1') where the previous output used %20, and that it still reads back as the same key.
uncertainty: Whether scheme names containing non-word characters (for example a dash as in 'my-app://') counted as protocol-bearing before this change is not shown by the supplied evidence; if any consumer builds such URLs, verify they are still treated as absolute rather than as relative paths.

report.summary: The URL utility toolkit was rebuilt end to end, changing how URLs are parsed, joined, normalized, encoded and how repeated query parameters are handled.
keyChanges: Joining, normalizing, parameter handling, slash cleanup and encoding now all flow through one shared URL object, so outputs and errors can differ from the previous release.

Joining a segment that carries its own protocol now fails with an explicit error instead of silently merging it; an appended segment's anchor (the #part) replaces the base URL's anchor, while later segments' query parameters still override earlier ones.

Repeated query names behave differently: '?tag=a&tag=b' now yields both values as a two-entry list instead of only the last value, and rebuilding such a URL keeps both pairs instead of collapsing them.

Generated URLs are now deliberately escaped: parameter names escape '=', '&' and '#' and render spaces as '+', values escape '#', '?' and '/' with spaces as %20, and a parameter supplied as a list is emitted as repeated pairs.
Normalizing a bare domain such as 'http://example.com' no longer appends a trailing slash, and non-string input (including URL objects previously accepted) now raises an explicit type error.
qaChecks: Verify joining a base URL with plain path segments produces single slashes and no doubled slashes: 'https://site.com/a' joined with 'b' and '/c' must give 'https://site.com/a/b/c'.

Test joining a segment that itself contains a protocol, for example base 'https://site.com/a' plus 'https://other.com/x': the new code must fail with an explicit error instead of silently merging the paths and parameters as it did before.

Verify parameters on later segments override the base's and an appended segment's anchor replaces the base's: 'https://site.com/a?id=1#h1' joined with 'b?id=2#h2' must give 'https://site.com/a/b?id=2#h2'.
Test a URL containing the same parameter twice, '?tag=a&tag=b': reading its parameters must now return both values as a two-entry list ('a' and 'b') rather than only the last value.

Verify rebuilding a URL that carries a repeated parameter keeps both pairs ('?tag=a&tag=b') instead of collapsing to the last value, whether the pairs came from the original URL or were passed in as a list of two values.
uncertainty: Generated query values do not escape a literal '&' while parameter names do, so one value like 'a&b' is emitted as 'k=a&b' and reads back as two parameters; confirm whether leaving '&' unescaped in values is intended.

report.summary: This release rebuilds the URL engine — a new URL class and a new query module replace the old URL class and the parameter helpers, which were renamed to query-based names — so URL parsing, query handling, and URL joining need regression testing, with credentials containing encoded colons as the top risk.
keyChanges: The old URL class was removed and replaced by a new one, the package's export list changed to match, and the helpers for reading and writing URL parameters were renamed from parameter-based names to query-based names, so any caller still using the old names or the old class will fail.

Query handling moved to a new dedicated module: repeated keys still read back as arrays of values, and a parameter whose value is empty or missing is written as a bare key with no equals sign (for example flag, not flag=).

Parsing now checks up front whether the input has a protocol and routes relative paths through a path-only branch, so the low-level parser now succeeds on relative inputs such as /only/path?a=1 where a direct call previously errored.

Credentials are now stored as one combined username:password string and re-split on the colon when read back; a username or password containing an encoded colon (%3A) is expected to be split at the wrong place (for example p%3Ass truncating to p), making this the release's most likely regression.
Hostname and port are now derived at read time by re-splitting one combined host string, so URLs with ports and percent-encoded host or credential characters should be re-verified end to end.
qaChecks: Verify http://user:pass@example.com/x reads back username 'user' and password 'pass' and its full URL output is still http://user:pass@example.com/x.

Test http://user:p%3Ass@example.com/x: the password should read back as 'p:ss' and the full URL output should keep it encoded as p%3Ass; if the password comes back truncated to 'p', the new combined credential handling has broken it.
Confirm http://example.com:3000/x?a=1 reports port '3000' and hostname 'example.com' and its full URL output still contains ':3000', the path, and the query.
Verify adding a parameter to a relative address without a protocol (input '/search?q=a' plus a new lang=en parameter) returns '/search?q=a&lang=en', staying relative with no host added.
Check a repeated key: reading '?tag=a&tag=b' returns both values, and writing tag as the array ['a','b'] produces 'tag=a&tag=b'.
uncertainty: Before this change, credentials were split on the colon before decoding, so a password written as p%3Ass survived parse-and-rebuild intact; the new code decodes the whole credential string first and then splits on the colon, so encoded colons inside usernames or passwords (and, more rarely, double-encoded characters in hosts) are expected to be mis-split or over-decoded. If any consumer relies on such credentials, confirm the intended behavior before release.

report.summary: This release rebuilds the URL utility library end to end, turning repeated query-parameter results into lists, tightening value encoding and input validation, changing join and normalization behavior, and reshaping the public exported helpers, so regression risk sits wherever URLs are built, joined, or read.
keyChanges: Query parameter parsing changed shape: a repeated key such as ?tag=a&tag=b now returns both values as a list instead of only the last one, and rewriting a URL's parameters now preserves both values instead of dropping the earlier duplicate.

Values are now explicitly encoded when a URL is rebuilt: spaces become +, a # stays inside the value as %23 instead of turning the remainder into the page fragment, and malformed percent signs like '100%' no longer throw an error.

Joining URL segments was rewritten: appending a segment that carries its own protocol such as 'https://other.com/x' now raises an error instead of being silently merged into the base path, and an appended fragment (#install) now replaces the base fragment (#intro) rather than being ignored.

Input handling tightened: non-string input now fails fast with a clear 'input should be string' error where the previous version accepted pre-parsed objects, and a protocol URL without a path now normalizes without a trailing slash (https://example.com instead of https://example.com/).

The public exported set was reshaped: the old URL-parsing helper, the old path-joining helper, and the old parsed-URL data shape were removed in favor of a new URL object and a consolidated set of re-exported helpers, so integrations still relying on the old exports must be migrated.
qaChecks: Verify reading the parameters of '?tag=a&tag=b' returns both values as a list (a and b), not only the last value b.
Test rewriting '/search?tag=a&tag=b' with an added parameter q=x produces '/search?tag=a&tag=b&q=x', keeping both tag values.
Ensure a value containing a space encodes as + ('my doc' becomes name=my+doc) and still reads back as 'my doc'.
Verify joining 'https://example.com/a', '/b', and '/c' produces 'https://example.com/a/b/c' with no doubled or missing slashes.

Test joining '/base' with a segment that carries its own protocol ('https://other.com/x') now fails with a clear error instead of silently producing '/base/x', and confirm no consumer flow shows an unhandled failure.
uncertainty: No application pages, roles, or flows were supplied for this URL utility library, so navigation was not found and verification is limited to the public helpers; the unresolved risk is whether existing consumers tolerate the new list-shaped values for repeated query keys, which previously arrived as a single last value.

report.summary: This release introduces new base-path and slash-detection URL utilities in the library and refactors the existing slash normalization to rely on them, with existing URL joining, resolution, and appending behavior intended to stay identical.
keyChanges: Two new utilities manage base paths: one adds a base prefix to a path unless the path already starts with that base, and one strips the base prefix, returning the root path '/' when the path equals the base exactly.

Two new boolean helpers detect whether a string has a trailing or leading slash, and the existing with/without slash normalization helpers now call them instead of checking inline; the checks are equivalent to the previous inline code, so no change in output is expected.

Because the refactored normalization feeds URL joining, path resolution, and URL appending, any difference in slash handling there would be a regression; the base-path helpers match the base as a plain string prefix, so paths sharing only the base's first characters are treated as already based.
qaChecks: Verify with base '/base' and path '/page' the add-base utility returns '/base/page', it returns '/base/page' unchanged when the path already starts with the base, and the strip-base utility turns '/base/page' back into '/page'.
Check a base supplied with a trailing slash ('/base/') behaves exactly like '/base': adding '/page' yields '/base/page' and stripping '/base/page' yields '/page'.

Confirm stripping a path equal to the base ('/base' with base '/base') returns the root path '/', and that a path merely starting with the same characters ('/baseball' with base '/base') is returned unchanged by the add-base utility.
Verify joining a base that ends with a slash to a path that starts with a slash (for example '/base/' joined with '/page') still produces '/base/page' with a single slash and no doubled slashes.

Confirm resolution and appending with edge inputs the old code handled specially (an empty string, a lone '/', and paths with slashes on both ends like '/a/b/') return exactly the same results as before this release.
uncertainty: The new base-path helpers match the base as a plain string prefix, so with base '/base' a path like '/baseball' is treated as already based and stripping cuts mid-segment; no documented rule was supplied to confirm segment-aware matching is intended, so confirm the desired behavior with the product owner.

report.summary: This URL-utility release adds slash-check predicates and new base-path prefix/strip helpers and rewrites the existing slash normalizers to use them with no behavior change; since no pages, routes, or navigation were supplied, QA verifies the helpers directly.
keyChanges: Two new exported predicates report whether a path ends or starts with a slash, and the three existing helpers that add or remove leading/trailing slashes now call them instead of checking inline; the logic is identical, so existing results should not change (an empty input still normalizes to '/', a lone '/' stays '/', and 'about' still becomes '/about').

A new helper adds a configured base path to any input that does not already start with it, and a companion helper removes that base and falls back to '/' when nothing is left; both first strip a trailing slash from the base, so a base like '/app/' works like '/app'.

URL joining, resolving, and same-path comparison flows sit downstream of these normalizers, so any slash-handling mistake would surface as doubled or missing slashes in produced URLs; none is expected because the rewrite preserves the previous logic.
qaChecks: Verify the trailing-slash remover still returns '/' for an empty input and for a lone '/', and turns 'about/' into 'about' while leaving 'about' unchanged.
Confirm the leading-slash adder and remover behave as before: '' becomes '/', '/' stays '/', and 'about' becomes '/about'.

Validate that URL joining and resolving still produce exactly one separating slash for mixed inputs, such as a base ending in '/' combined with a path starting with '/', with no doubled or missing slash.
Test the base-prefix helper with base '/app': 'about' should become '/app/about', while an input already under the base, '/app/about', should come back unchanged.
Confirm a base supplied with a trailing slash, '/app/', behaves the same as '/app' because the base is trimmed before comparison and joining.
uncertainty: The rewritten slash normalizers test exactly what the inline code tested before, so no input was found that changes existing behavior and regression risk there is low; the unresolved point is whether the new base helpers should match on full path segments rather than shared characters, since an input that merely begins with the base's characters is treated as already based and, when stripping, leaves only the leftover characters.

report.summary: The URL utility library gains new public helpers for detecting leading and trailing slashes and for attaching or stripping a configured base path, while three existing slash helpers now delegate to the new detectors with no intended behavior change.
keyChanges: New base path helpers attach or remove a base: attaching ignores any trailing slash on the base, returns the path unchanged when it already begins with the base, and otherwise joins base and path; removing strips the base from the front and returns / when nothing remains besides the base.
New helpers also report whether a path has a leading or trailing slash, returning false for an empty value or a call with no argument.

Three existing slash helpers now call the new detectors instead of checking strings inline; the checks are logically identical, so every input should produce the same result as before, including empty input, which still falls back to /.

These helpers sit behind URL joining, URL resolution, path comparison, and appending to a URL, so those capabilities should behave exactly as before; automated suites for joining, base handling, resolution, and slash handling are in place as coverage evidence.

report.summary: This release rewrites the URL library's core internals and public surface: the old URL class and params helpers are replaced by a new URL class plus a dedicated query module, so behavior should stay equivalent but every import path changed.
keyChanges: The old URL class, which exposed hostname, port, username, password and params as direct fields, was deleted and replaced by a new URL class that stores raw host and auth strings and derives hostname, port, username, password, query and search on demand; protocol-less input is now short-circuited to path-only parsing.

Query handling moved to a new module replacing the old params parsing and serialization: repeated keys still become arrays and falsy values still serialize as bare keys, but empty key entries produced by a trailing or doubled ampersand are now dropped where the old code kept a blank entry.

The params-based helpers for reading and merging parameters were removed and replaced by query-based equivalents with the same merge-and-rebuild flow, preserving behavior while changing names and value shapes.

Public exports changed: the old class name and the params helpers are no longer exported, and the new URL class and query helpers are exported instead, which is a breaking change for consumers using the old names.

The new code decodes raw values without the old empty-string fallbacks, so inputs that previously guaranteed empty strings, such as usernames without passwords and protocol-less paths, must be re-verified to yield empty parts rather than errors or the text 'undefined'.
qaChecks: Verify that reading parameters from '?a=1&a=2&b=3' returns a as both values (1 and 2) and b as the single string 3.

Test a query string with a trailing ampersand or an empty '&&' segment, for example '/search?q=x&': valid keys must still be read, and rebuilding the URL must not emit a stray empty entry such as '=undefined' or a blank segment, which the previous implementation could produce.

Confirm that merging new parameters into a URL that already has parameters keeps existing keys unless they are overridden, and that a key-only parameter such as '?flag' serializes back as the bare key 'flag' without '='.

Confirm that 'https://user:pass@shop.example.com:8443/products?q=1#reviews' parses into the expected protocol, host, port, username, password, path, query and hash, and that rebuilding returns an equivalent URL.
Test a URL with a username but no password in the address, for example 'http://user@example.com/x': the password part must come back empty, not the text 'undefined'.
uncertainty: The old code applied empty-string fallbacks before decoding missing parts, while the new code decodes the raw value first and the decoder's handling of undefined values is not visible in the supplied evidence; if the decoder stringifies undefined, protocol-less URLs or username-only auth would report 'undefined' parts or throw, and the checks above target exactly those inputs.

report.summary: This release rebuilds the URL toolkit's core object and query engine, concentrating risk in URL parsing, normalization, resolution, and query-string reading and writing.
keyChanges: The URL object class was rewritten end to end: input must be a string (anything else raises a clear type error), protocol-less input is now detected inside the parser and treated as a relative path, and the parsed result exposes protocol, host, credentials, path, a query object, and hash that together rebuild the URL string.

Query handling moved to a new engine: parsing splits on ampersand and equals signs, decodes keys and values, collects repeated keys into ordered lists, and now skips entries with no key (for example '?=x' or a trailing '&') that the previous version returned under an empty name.
Query serialization renders an empty or omitted value as a bare key (so '?a=' round-trips to '?a') and repeats the key once per value in a list.

The public API changed: the old parameter helpers were removed in favor of query-based ones; adding query values to a URL keeps the URL's existing query with provided keys winning, and it now also works for relative URLs; the old URL class is no longer exported while the new URL class and the query helpers are.

URL resolution and normalization now run through the new class: joined paths keep a single slash between segments, the appended URL's hash wins, and appending a URL that itself carries a protocol is rejected with an error.
qaChecks: Verify reading the query from 'http://example.com/?=x&a=1' ignores the keyless entry and returns only a=1, and adding b=2 to the same input returns 'http://example.com/?a=1&b=2' with no stray '=x' fragment.
Check reading the query from 'http://example.com/?a=1&a=2' returns both values for a, in order, as a list of two entries.

Test adding the values b=new and c='' (an empty string) to 'http://example.com/?a=1&b=old' returns 'http://example.com/?a=1&b=new&c', where provided keys replace existing ones and the empty value renders as a bare key.
Ensure adding the query q=x to the relative path '/search' returns '/search?q=x', proving relative URLs are now supported.

Verify parsing 'http://user:pass@example.com:8080/p?q=1#h' reads back protocol, hostname, port, username, password, path, query and hash correctly, and the rebuilt string is 'http://user:pass@example.com:8080/p?q=1#h'.
uncertainty: The old protocol-detection rule is not part of the supplied evidence, so it cannot be confirmed whether schemes containing characters outside letters, digits and underscore (for example 'web+store://host') were recognized as absolute URLs before this change; the new behavior treats them as relative paths, which consumers relying on the old recognition should verify.
